title: [High][BUILD-001] Desktop WebView POM hard-codes the publisher OS in JavaFX dependencies
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:BUILD-001 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** BUILD-001
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** L
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/build.gradle.kts:9-18`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/build.gradle.kts#L9-L18) — `platform`
- [`calf-webview/build.gradle.kts:41-47`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/build.gradle.kts#L41-L47) — `desktopMain.dependencies`

## Root cause
The desktop dependency classifiers are chosen from OperatingSystem.current() and os.arch during producer configuration, not the consumer runtime or a published OS-specific variant.

## Impact and preconditions
The same calf-webview-desktop coordinate encodes one operating system. A consumer on another OS receives the wrong JavaFX native artifacts unless it overrides dependency selection. The audit-generated Linux POM proves host capture; a cross-OS application launch was not executed.

## Supporting evidence
- Baseline local task :calf-webview:generatePomFileForDesktopPublication passed; no publication occurred
- docs/testing/evidence/baseline-webview-desktop-linux.pom contains classifier linux on all six JavaFX 19 modules
- docs/testing/evidence/baseline-task-inventory-and-webview-pom.log records the successful command

## Recommended solution
Model OS/architecture-aware desktop variants or require an explicit consumer JavaFX runtime dependency. Keep JavaFX modules aligned and add isolated published-metadata consumer fixtures for Linux/macOS/Windows; do not simply replace every classifier with the current migration host.

## Risks and compatibility
Changing Maven/Gradle metadata can affect existing consumers and duplicate transitive JavaFX modules. Validate both POM-only and Gradle-module-metadata clients.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Generate POM and Gradle module metadata on two different hosts and compare dependency selectors
- Resolve and launch a desktop WebView consumer on Linux x64, macOS arm64/x64 and Windows x64
- Verify native classifier availability for every advertised architecture

## Dependencies
- None identified.

title: [High][BUILD-003] Any nonempty prebuilt native subdirectory suppresses every local native build
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:BUILD-003 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** BUILD-003
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker`, `calf-share`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/build.gradle.kts:33-39`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/build.gradle.kts#L33-L39) — `hasPrebuiltNativeLibs`
- [`calf-share/build.gradle.kts:29-33`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/build.gradle.kts#L29-L33) — `hasPrebuiltNativeLibs`

## Root cause
The prebuilt predicate accepts any nonempty immediate directory. It does not check the host target, expected library filename, source revision, JNI ABI, package version, checksum, or complete publication platform matrix.

## Impact and preconditions
A partial/stale/foreign-platform artifact folder silently bypasses Rust compilation and is packaged as trusted resources. Desktop consumers can fail with missing native libraries or receive binaries unrelated to the checked-out Kotlin/Rust source. This is an integrity/release-readiness defect, not evidence of malicious binaries.

## Supporting evidence
- The exact predicates contain only exists/isDirectory/listFiles().isNotEmpty checks
- The Rust build/copy tasks are entirely absent when the predicate is true

## Recommended solution
Introduce a native artifact manifest keyed by module, target, source revision and ABI/version; validate required filenames and checksums before skipping a build. Use explicit developer-host vs release-matrix tasks and fail closed for incomplete release inputs.

## Risks and compatibility
Must preserve offline/prebuilt developer workflows and distinguish source builds from full release assemblies. A checksum manifest must itself be tied to trusted CI provenance.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Test empty, irrelevant-file-only, wrong-platform, corrupt, stale-revision and missing-library directories
- Verify full artifact manifests before assembling candidate desktop JARs
- Load each candidate binary and check JNI symbol compatibility on its intended host

## Dependencies
- None identified.

- [`convention-plugins/src/main/kotlin/Android.kt:33-37`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/convention-plugins/src/main/kotlin/Android.kt#L33-L37) — `withHostTest`
- [`convention-plugins/src/main/kotlin/Targets.kt:11-22`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/convention-plugins/src/main/kotlin/Targets.kt#L11-L22) — `declared targets`

## Root cause
Only 86 upstream Kotlin @Test functions exist (69 UI, 9 picker, 6 IO, 2 navigation), with no Rust test functions, Android device tests or iOS-specific test sources. The baseline main CI runs allTests on one macOS host and compiles native libraries without behavioral tests. No API/ABI snapshot or external consumer gate is configured.

## Impact and preconditions
A green task aggregate cannot establish platform parity, JNI lifecycle safety, Android permissions/device behavior, iOS delegate correctness, browser functionality, or binary/source compatibility. The audit found real defects in areas outside this test surface.

## Supporting evidence
- docs/testing/evidence/baseline-test-inventory.json enumerates all 86 annotations in 13 executable test files plus 2 helper files
- Both native src/lib.rs files contain zero #[test] annotations
- Baseline build workflow invokes only ./gradlew allTests; no external consumer fixture or device runner is configured

## Recommended solution
Create layered CI: common unit tests; Linux/macOS/Windows desktop tests and native smoke tests; JS/Wasm browser tests; Android host plus device/API-matrix tests; Apple simulator/device lifecycle tests; sample builds; candidate-artifact consumer and API/ABI compatibility checks. Retain machine-readable results and distinguish NO-SOURCE/SKIPPED from tests passed.

## Risks and compatibility
GUI tests require deterministic dialogs, timezone, locale and UI-thread scheduling. A much larger matrix should be phased by risk and avoid publishing as part of verification.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Verify per-module test counts are nonzero where expected
- Exercise all regressions listed in module finding required_tests
- Build isolated minimum-supported-SDK and Kotlin/Compose-version consumers
- Assert Kotlin/JNI/Swift API compatibility against the retained compatibility surface

title: [High][IO-001] iOS byte-array reads can overrun native destination memory and mishandle empty files
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-001 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-001
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-io`, `calf-file-picker-coil`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt:35-41`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt#L35-L41) — `KmpFile.readByteArray`
- [`calf-file-picker-coil/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/coil/KmpFileFetcher.kt:22-27`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker-coil/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/coil/KmpFileFetcher.kt#L22-L27) — `KmpFileFetcher.fetch`

## Root cause
The ByteArray allocation clamps NSData.length to Int.MAX_VALUE, but memcpy still receives the original, larger length. The zero-length case unconditionally calls addressOf(0).

## Impact and preconditions
For a file larger than Int.MAX_VALUE whose allocations succeed, native writes exceed the Kotlin buffer. Empty data violates the element-address precondition. Coil reaches this path too. This is memory-unsafety in source, not a demonstrated device exploit.

## Supporting evidence
- Baseline lines 37 and 40 use different allocation/copy lengths. No guard precedes addressOf(0).
- Linux cannot execute Foundation or Kotlin/Native iOS behavior. The unsafe arithmetic is source-confirmed.
- The archived PR #551 branch retains this memcpy pattern; its other IO changes do not fix this finding.

## Recommended solution
Return immediately for length zero, reject lengths exceeding the representable ByteArray limit before allocating, copy exactly the validated allocation size, and prefer source() for large content. Make NSData read failure an explicit error.

## Risks and compatibility
Native bounds fixes must preserve byte signedness and all platforms' exception contracts. Large-file tests must not exhaust devices; use a checked-length helper and controlled native fixtures.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Zero-byte valid file
- One-byte and binary round trips
- Length helper at Int.MAX_VALUE and Int.MAX_VALUE+1 without huge allocations
- Missing/unreadable file errors
- ASan/native guarded-buffer integration where supported
- Coil error propagation

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/pull/551

title: [High][IO-002] Android saver loses pending content across recomposition and can report an empty export as success
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-002 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-002
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.android.kt:31-32`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.android.kt#L31-L32) — `pendingSource`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.android.kt:34-60`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.android.kt#L34-L60) — `ActivityResult callback`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.android.kt:65-74`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.android.kt#L65-L74) — `remembered launch lambdas`

## Root cause
remember<Any?> { null } remembers null, not a mutable holder. Each recomposition creates a new local variable/reference cell. The once-remembered launcher assigns the initial cell while rememberLauncherForActivityResult updates to a callback capturing the latest cell.

## Impact and preconditions
After recomposition while the save sheet is open, source is null and the write branch is skipped; onResult still returns KmpFile(uri). ByteArray and KmpFile exports can silently produce zero-byte documents. Pending sources also lack a process-recreation policy and are not cleared.

## Supporting evidence
- The Kotlin capture structure is directly visible at lines 32,42,65-73.
- Unmerged upstream commit be274cc530ff92e6e3bde9ac0ffbb912d5e3068a independently describes this exact recomposition defect and adds host tests; those tests were not run here.

## Recommended solution
Store a PendingSaveRequest in a remembered state/holder shared by launch and callback. Consume and clear exactly once; define process-death recovery separately for URI and in-memory payloads; fail/clean up rather than returning success when required content is unavailable.

## Risks and compatibility
Do not put large ByteArrays in saved-instance Bundle state. Serialize concurrent launch attempts, and distinguish intentional null/empty content from lost pending state.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Compose/Robolectric launch, recompose, then result for bytes and KmpFile
- Activity recreation with pending URI and ByteArray
- Cancel clears payload
- Repeated/concurrent launch policy
- No-op write cannot report success

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/pull/551
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/commit/be274cc530ff92e6e3bde9ac0ffbb912d5e3068a

title: [High][IO-003] Desktop composition disposal races raw JNI handles; cancelled creation can leak handles
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-003 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-003
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** L
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.desktop.kt:98-145`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.desktop.kt#L98-L145) — `LaunchedEffect and DisposableEffect`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.desktop.kt:152-166`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.desktop.kt#L152-L166) — `launch under dialogMutex`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/platform/PlatformFilePicker.kt:79-89`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/platform/PlatformFilePicker.kt#L79-L89) — `showFilePicker/showDirectoryPicker`
- [`calf-file-picker/native/src/lib.rs:254-272`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/native/src/lib.rs#L254-L272) — `box_config/ref_config/drop_config`
- [`calf-file-picker/native/src/lib.rs:379-384,408-410,443-450`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/native/src/lib.rs#L379-L384) — `JNI show/destroy exports`

## Root cause
Launch and settings updates use dialogMutex, but onDispose destroys the same pointer without that mutex or a native ownership registry. A queued/starting IO show call can dereference freed DialogConfig memory. A handle allocated inside withContext(IO) is not yet owned by dialogHandle if prompt cancellation discards its return value.

## Impact and preconditions
Disposal interleaving with queued show/config.build can cause use-after-free and process crashes; panic catching does not make invalid pointer dereferences safe. Rapid settings changes/disposal during creation can leak native allocations. launch() before initial creation silently returns without a callback.

## Supporting evidence
- onDispose at 138-144 does not acquire dialogMutex, while launch holds it at 153.
- Rust ref_config blindly dereferences handle and manufactures a static reference; drop_config frees it.
- Source establishes the unsafe interleaving; no native GUI/race exploit was executed.

## Recommended solution
Introduce one owner for each dialog session: acquire/close/show via a safe handle registry or equivalent lifetime mechanism; mark disposed and serialize destruction with in-flight use. Ensure allocation cleanup on cancelled delivery, and queue or explicitly reject launch before readiness. Preserve the existing public API where possible.

## Risks and compatibility
Do not block the UI waiting for a user to close a native dialog. A raw pointer is not made safe by a Kotlin mutex unless every destructor participates; cancellation is not native-dialog termination.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Deterministically pause IO show before JNI entry then dispose
- Dispose while config.build runs under ASan/Valgrind
- Cancel each creation handoff boundary and count allocations/frees
- Repeated settings changes + double launch
- Launch immediately after composition
- Window closes with dialog visible

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- None identified.

title: [High][IO-004] Desktop save can delete its own source and does not reliably replace existing content
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-004 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-004
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/platform/PlatformFilePicker.kt:95-115`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/platform/PlatformFilePicker.kt#L95-L115) — `showSaveDialog/showSaveDialogWithFile`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.kt:31-49`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.kt#L31-L49) — `launch content contract`

## Root cause
The file overload uses sourceFile.copyTo(destFile, overwrite=true) without same-file detection; Kotlin deletes an existing target before opening the source. For identical paths this deletes the source. The null-content overload calls createNewFile(), which does nothing when a target already exists.

## Impact and preconditions
Choosing the source file as the destination destroys the only source and then raises FileNotFoundException. Saving null to an existing nonempty destination returns success while preserving its old contents instead of the documented empty-file semantics. Other failed overwrites can leave a deleted or partial destination.

## Supporting evidence
- scripts/audit/io_jvm_probes.py compiled the unchanged baseline PlatformFilePicker.kt with a fake native dialog returning a temporary source path.
- Observed FileNotFoundException and source.exists=false after self-copy.
- Observed 13 old bytes still present after a successful null-content save.
- The same harness passed normal copy/cancel/new-empty-file paths on installed Kotlin2.0.21/coroutines1.6.4 and Kotlin2.4.0/coroutines1.10.2; this was not the pinned full Gradle build.

## Recommended solution
Detect same files with filesystem identity checks (including aliases) before destructive work, define a no-op or explicit error for self-copy, and implement deliberate overwrite semantics. Stage content into a sibling temporary file and replace atomically where possible; explicitly truncate if null is defined as empty content.

## Risks and compatibility
Consider symlinks, hard links, permission changes, atomic-move availability and cancellation. The reproduction used only audit-owned temporary files. Do not add file deletion to a generic error path without proving ownership.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Source equals destination
- Relative/absolute alias, symlink and hard-link destinations
- Null content with existing and absent target
- Read/write failure preserves old destination
- Large streamed copy and cancellation
- Normal save/cancel

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- None identified.

- [`calf-file-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.picker/FileSaverLauncher.ios.kt:119-123`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.picker/FileSaverLauncher.ios.kt#L119-L123) — `writeTempFile`

## Root cause
The KmpFile overload passes file.url directly, ignoring baseName/extension. The byte/data path prefixes the requested filename with a UUID in the filename itself. The one-argument forExportingURLs initializer uses move-style export instead of explicitly selecting asCopy=true.

## Impact and preconditions
The Save API can offer Move and transfer the source rather than leave it intact. Exported names can unexpectedly contain UUID prefixes or retain the original source name. Saved KmpFiles may also point outside ongoing security-scoped access.

- Baseline passes file.url directly at 109 and constructs UUID-filename at 120.
- Unmerged commits 675d049 and be274cc in PR #551 implement named staging and asCopy=true; their existence corroborates the baseline defect, not its repair on main.
- No iOS device run was available.

## Recommended solution
Stage all exports in a unique private directory under the exact requested basename, preserve source contents, use the explicit copy export initializer, and remove only owned staging after terminal completion. Validate/normalize filename components.

## Risks and compatibility
Staging adds disk IO but not whole-file heap buffering. Handle scope acquisition and failure before presenting a picker. Prevent path separators from escaping or corrupting the staging layout.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Verify source remains after successful save
- Bytes/NSData/KmpFile/NSURL export has exact suggested name
- Cancel and interactive dismissal cleanup
- Unicode and separator-containing names
- Read-only/disk-full staging
- Destination access after callback

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-001 -->
## Classification

- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)

- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.desktop.kt:225-248`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.desktop.kt#L225-L248) — `WebViewNavigator.handleNavigationEvents / StopLoading`
- [`calf-webview/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.kt:248-249`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.kt#L248-L249) — `WebViewNavigator.stopLoading`

## Root cause
Inside with(webView.engine), unqualified stopLoading() has no matching WebEngine member and resolves to the enclosing WebViewNavigator.stopLoading(). That emits another StopLoading event, which queues another Platform.runLater callback.

## Impact and preconditions
One stop request produces an unbounded coroutine/FX event feedback loop while the collector lives, consumes CPU, and does not stop the network/page load. Replayed commands can restart it after attachment.

## Supporting evidence
- docs/testing/native-features-probes/results-baseline.json: STOP_FEEDBACK steps=100 queued=1 nativeCancels=0.
- Dependency evidence identifies JavaFX19 WebEngine private stop(), reached by loadWorker.cancel(), not a public stopLoading API.
- git log -S stopLoading() traces the call back to the initial separate webview artifact; later FX-thread fixes retained it.

## Recommended solution
Call webView.engine.loadWorker.cancel() explicitly on the FX thread. Use explicit native receivers for each branch and ensure stop produces no new navigation event.

## Risks and compatibility
Probe replaces the FX engine and queue, not a running JavaFX GUI; the exact handler and navigator bodies were compiled. Public JavaFX19 source confirms absence of stopLoading. Do not describe this as a passed Desktop integration test.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Assert a single stop request calls the native worker cancel once and emits no further commands.
- Run slow-page loading, stop, detach/reattach, and repeated-stop cases in an actual JavaFX/Compose window.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

title: [High][NATIVE-002] Android and Desktop WebViews retain live native views after composition disposal
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-002 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-002
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/web/WebView.android.kt:194-215,405-408`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/web/WebView.android.kt#L194-L215) — `AndroidView.factory/onRelease and WebViewState.webView`
- [`calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.desktop.kt:52-108,211-212`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.desktop.kt#L52-L108) — `DisposableEffect/onDispose and WebViewState.webView`

## Root cause
Android onRelease only calls the user callback; it neither stops/destroys the WebView nor clears state.webView/clients. Desktop onDispose only calls the user callback; it leaves scene, engine load, listeners and state.webView connected, with implicit FX exit disabled.

## Impact and preconditions
When callers retain WebViewState, it retains the Android Activity/view or the entire Desktop WebView/scene and callbacks after the UI is removed. Loading, audio/timers and native resources may outlive the screen; old views can be observed during remount.

## Supporting evidence
- Android line209 stores state.webView; line213 is the sole onRelease action.
- Desktop line101 stores state.webView and lines60-98 register strong closures; lines105-107 do not undo either.

## Recommended solution
Define ownership and teardown ordering: save state first, cancel load, detach clients/listeners, remove scene/native references, destroy Android WebView after removal, and clear state.webView if it still denotes that instance. Put cleanup in finally so a throwing user onDispose cannot skip it. Manage FX runtime lifetime independently rather than exiting per view.

## Risks and compatibility
Missing teardown and retained references are source-confirmed; actual retained heap size, active playback and host process shutdown depend on engine/application behavior. Do not invoke private JavaFX dispose APIs without support analysis.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Retain state, mount/unmount repeatedly and verify Activity/native view collectability with weak references/profilers.
- Verify teardown cancels a slow request and media and does not clear a replacement instance.
- Test onDispose throwing, delayed Platform.runLater initialization, process-state save and multiwindow operation.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

title: [High][NATIVE-010] Enabling Web JavaScript removes all iframe isolation for inline HTML
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-010 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-010
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt:57-58,169-176,225-226`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt#L57-L58) — `HTML content and iframe.applySettings`

## Root cause
javaScriptEnabled=true removes the sandbox attribute entirely. srcdoc then inherits the host origin; scripts in supplied inline HTML can access the parent DOM, same-origin storage and host-page capabilities. There is no separate sandbox/origin policy in the common API.

## Impact and preconditions
If an application renders untrusted HTML with JavaScript enabled, content that would be isolated inside a native WebView instead obtains the browser host application origin. A browser probe changed the host DOM using only child script; exploitation requires attacker-controlled HTML and the explicit JS opt-in.

## Supporting evidence
- Real Chrome153 probe unsandboxedSrcdocCanModifyHost=true using a local harmless parent attribute change.
- Disabled mode sets sandbox without allow-scripts; enabled mode removes every sandbox restriction.

## Recommended solution
Expose a distinct sandbox/trusted-content policy with safe defaults; for untrusted HTML use an opaque-origin sandbox allowing only needed capabilities and a validated postMessage bridge. Warn that enabling scripts is not merely toggling execution in an isolated native container.

## Risks and compatibility
This is not an unconditional XSS or sandbox bypass: default JavaScript is false, normal cross-origin pages still have same-origin restrictions, and browser CSP may constrain effects. allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin for same-origin/srcdoc content is not robust isolation.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Untrusted inline script cannot read/mutate parent DOM or storage under isolated mode.
- Trusted mode preserves deliberate integration and is explicitly opted into.
- Test popups/forms/top navigation, nested frames, postMessage origin validation and CSP.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

title: [High][NATIVE-013] Desktop CookieManager overwrites JavaFX and application-global cookie handlers
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-013 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-013
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.desktop.kt:13-20`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.desktop.kt#L13-L20) — `cookieManager getter`

## Root cause
Any default CookieHandler not deriving from java.net.CookieManager is replaced by a new empty java.net.CookieManager. JavaFX19 WebPage normally installs com.sun.webkit.network.CookieManager, which extends CookieHandler directly, so even a first read can replace the active WebKit cookie store. Application custom handlers are likewise replaced.

## Impact and preconditions
Cookie operations can discard access to existing login cookies and change networking behavior for every component using the process-global handler. JavaFX uses special javascript/javascripts schemes for document.cookie filtering, so substituting an unrelated handler also requires semantic compatibility review.

## Supporting evidence
- Standalone actual CookieManager probe COOKIE_HANDLER_REPLACED true.
- JavaFX19 WebPage.java141-146 installs com.sun.webkit.network.CookieManager; that class extends CookieHandler, not java.net.CookieManager.

## Recommended solution
Do not mutate global state during a getter. Establish explicit cookie-store ownership at toolkit initialization, preserve/adapt compatible handlers, or expose a deliberate application-supplied backend. Handle JavaFX’s store and concurrent access without silently replacing it.

## Risks and compatibility
A custom-handler replacement was executed against the actual Kotlin cookie class. JavaFX default installation/type were verified in the exact 19 source archive; loss of a real logged-in JavaFX session remains a required GUI integration test. No private com.sun API adoption without maintenance assessment.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Login in a real WebEngine, call getCookies, then ensure session and handler identity remain valid.
- Install a custom CookieHandler before creation and verify library does not overwrite it.
- Two managers accessed concurrently and secure/HttpOnly document.cookie behavior under the chosen backend.

- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)

The pending image URI is stored only inside a newly remembered CameraPickerLauncherAndroidImpl. ActivityResultRegistry can deliver a restored TakePicture Boolean, but the recreated instance has imageUri=null and drops the successful result.

This is a source-traced lifecycle defect; no Android device/emulator Activity recreation test was run by this reviewer. Do not persist a granted URI longer than its actual access lifetime without an ownership policy.

title: [High][NATIVE-027] Desktop share fallback opens arbitrary files/URLs instead of offering an explicit sharing fallback
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-027 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-027
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-share`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-share/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/ShareLauncher.desktop.kt:51-64,108-155`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/ShareLauncher.desktop.kt#L51-L64) — `handleShare/shareUrlFallback/shareFileFallback/shareFilesFallback`

## Root cause
On Windows/Linux or any native-share failure, URLs are sent to Desktop.browse and files to Desktop.open with no MIME, URI-scheme or executable/handler policy. This occurs automatically after swallowed native errors, not after a separate open/preview decision.

## Impact and preconditions
A user asking to share can instead launch a registered URL handler or open an untrusted file in an associated application. Depending on OS associations, opening executable/script/shortcut content can run code; many files can launch many apps. No code execution exploit was demonstrated and user-supplied content/control of the call are required.

## Supporting evidence
- shareFileFallback calls desktop.open(file) at132; Files repeats it at147.
- MIME type passed in ShareContent.File/Files is not used by Desktop fallback.

## Recommended solution
Make fallback behavior explicit/opt-in. Prefer Unavailable, copying shareable data, or a documented export/open-location action over automatically opening content. Validate supported URL schemes and avoid executing/previewing untrusted files as an incidental share operation.

## Risks and compatibility
Current docs disclose opening default apps on Windows/Linux, so this is a safety/design risk rather than hidden malicious behavior. Removing it can be a user-visible compatibility change; offer a policy parameter and deprecation path.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- With OS open/browse calls mocked, file share does not execute/open without chosen policy.
- Native-loader failure follows the same safe fallback as unsupported OS.
- Untrusted file extensions/custom URI schemes and multi-file partial failure produce a truthful result without unintended handlers.

navigate(route, arguments) appends only the route String. No entry or argument payload is stored; the host passes the graph destination's static Map<String, NavArgument> definition to content instead of a navigation entry's values.

## Impact and preconditions
Callers cannot send different argument values to two visits of the same route. The API accepts input that is never observed; saved/restored stacks likewise carry no arguments. The module is currently unpublished, which limits consumer exposure but not the defect.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Controller line24 uses only backStack.add(route).
- Host line43 calls destination.content(destination.arguments); there is no lookup of the navigate arguments parameter.
- No route interpolation/deep-link argument parser is wired into AdaptiveNavHost.

## Recommended solution
Before stabilizing or publishing navigation, define a typed entry/payload contract distinct from argument schema; validate and merge defaults at navigation, expose resolved values to content, and implement a save/restore policy. Preserve or deprecate the current overload explicitly rather than silently dropping inputs.

## Risks and compatibility
Changing public types and saver format affects callers and restoration; do not hide the change in the identity migration. Never persist secrets or arbitrary unserializable objects by default.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Navigate to one route with two distinct payloads; each visit receives its own values.
- Validate missing, nullable, wrong-type and defaulted arguments.
- Round-trip entry IDs and arguments through the saver; reject unsupported values predictably.

## Root cause
The stack permits duplicate strings, but the state provider key is currentDestination (route) and popped-state cleanup compares sets of routes. There is no unique navigation-entry identity.

## Impact and preconditions
A -> B -> A reuses the first A's saveable state; A -> A can keep the same composition. Popping one occurrence while another remains cannot discard only the popped entry's state. A pop/re-push between observed compositions is also invisible to route-set cleanup.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Provider key at line42 is the route string; cleanup at line56 drops multiplicity via toSet().
- The two baseline tests exercise home/detail with distinct routes only.
- Archived #542 commit1554f1b7758e634faf93cd4e851046b94b3fb954 introduced route-keyed retention; no duplicate-entry test is present.

## Recommended solution
Give each stack entry a stable unique ID, key state and cleanup by that ID, persist it with the entry, and prune state for removed entries. Retain the positive distinct-route behavior introduced by #542.

## Risks and compatibility
Saver compatibility and lifecycle expectations must be specified. A route-key optimization is not equivalent to Jetpack Navigation's per-entry owners. Compose/device reproduction remains required; this finding is based on the explicit identity algorithm.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- A -> B -> A has two independent counters and popping restores the original A.
- Consecutive A -> A produces fresh local/saveable entry state.
- Pop and immediately push the same route before an idle frame; the new entry is fresh.
- Restore a stack containing duplicate routes and pop each independently.
- Retain both existing #542 tests.

Reverse mapping selects firstOrNull from the global registry. Gallery and ReadStorage both map to READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE on API<=32. Registration order is unrelated to the active request; updatePermissionsStatus only refreshes the matching logical permission.

Requesting Gallery after ReadStorage was initialized can report ReadStorage instead, omit Gallery, and leave its status stale. Requesting both refreshes only one alias; custom aliases have the same problem.

- Compiled unmodified AndroidPermissionRegistry plus extracted original Permission and mapping helpers with a Build.VERSION stub; at SDK32 a result for requested Gallery became {ReadStorage=true}.
- This test validates Kotlin mapping, not an Android permission dialog.

## Recommended solution
Convert each result using the request-scoped logical-permission-to-native-string mapping; fan a native result out to every requested logical alias, deduplicate native strings, and never substitute an unrelated global alias.

## Risks and compatibility
Callback maps may expand for callers that accidentally depended on one alias. Include SDK ranges and empty/not-applicable permissions without reintroducing empty launcher inputs.

- Initialize ReadStorage then request only Gallery; reverse the initialization order.
- Request both aliases and assert both state objects and callback entries.

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:PERM-004 -->
## Classification

- **Priority:** High

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.android.kt:90-99`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.android.kt#L90-L99) — `launchPermissionRequest`

- [`calf-permissions/location/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/LocationPermissions.android.kt:5-21`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/location/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/LocationPermissions.android.kt#L5-L21) — `registerFineLocationPermission/registerCoarseLocationPermission`
- [`calf-permissions/background-location/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/BackgroundLocationPermissions.android.kt:5-12`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/background-location/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/BackgroundLocationPermissions.android.kt#L5-L12) — `registerBackgroundLocationPermission`

## Root cause
A logical permission maps to exactly one string; FineLocation alone requests only ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION. Bulk dispatch sends all strings together without separating background location from foreground permissions or checking prerequisites.

## Impact and preconditions
Android12+ requires requesting FINE together with COARSE for precise access; requesting fine alone may be ignored. Android11+ foreground and background location cannot be requested together; background requires an already-granted foreground path and settings-oriented UX. Common single-fine/sample bulk patterns do not implement these rules.

## Supporting evidence
- Source sends one native string for FineLocation and an unpartitioned array for all bulk permissions.
- Android platform guidance: https://developer.android.com/develop/sensors-and-location/location/permissions/runtime and /background.

## Recommended solution
Add a tested location request strategy (fine+coarse in one foreground step, then a separate background step with target-SDK-appropriate education/settings); or explicitly reject/document unsupported combinations until that API exists. Preserve approximate grants rather than treating coarse-only as total failure.

## Risks and compatibility
OS and target-SDK dependent; precise dialog/device behavior was not executed in this Linux audit. Never silently escalate a coarse-only request to precise/background access.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- API23,29,30,31,33+ with both current and legacy targetSdk: fine alone, coarse alone, fine+coarse, foreground+background.
- Accept approximate, deny precise, deny background and return from Settings.
- Verify manifest omissions and location services disabled are distinguished.

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:PERM-008 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** PERM-008
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-permissions/core`
- **Estimated complexity:** L

- [`calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/MutableMultiplePermissionsState.ios.kt:45-53,88-91`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/MutableMultiplePermissionsState.ios.kt#L45-L53) — `rememberMutablePermissionsState/launchMultiplePermissionRequest`

launchMultiplePermissionRequest loops synchronously over helpers that start asynchronous native requests. Each helper invokes onPermissionsResult(mapOf(permission to result)); there is no queue, deduplication by native domain, batch map, or completion barrier.

Clients cannot consume one complete batch like on Android. Different native prompts contend, location prerequisite order is lost, and aliases create multiple simultaneous helpers for the same OS domain. Empty batches never invoke a callback.

Serialize prompt-producing requests, deduplicate equivalent native authorizations, aggregate results keyed by every requested logical permission, and define empty/cancelled batch completion. Keep progress callbacks separate if desired.

## Risks and compatibility
Source confirms concurrent dispatch and singleton callbacks. Exact prompt collision behavior varies by Apple API and needs device verification. Callback-contract changes should be documented as a behavioral correction.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Camera+microphone, fine+coarse, foreground+background, Gallery+ReadImage and Notification+RemoteNotification batches.

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:PERM-009 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** PERM-009
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-permissions/background-location`, `calf-permissions/core`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-permissions/background-location/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/helper/BackgroundLocationPermissionHelper.kt:25-50`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/background-location/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/helper/BackgroundLocationPermissionHelper.kt#L25-L50) — `launchPermissionRequest/getPermissionStatus`
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/helper/PermissionHelper.kt:20-29`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/helper/PermissionHelper.kt#L20-L29) — `handleLaunchPermissionRequest`

## Root cause
AuthorizedWhenInUse falls through to Denied(shouldShowRationale=true). The shared handler interprets that as permanently denied and immediately invokes false; requestAlwaysAuthorization is only reached for NotDetermined.

## Impact and preconditions
The normal staged foreground-to-background authorization upgrade is blocked by library logic, independently of OS dialog scheduling. Existing foreground grants can never request Always through this helper.

## Supporting evidence
- The actual baseline BackgroundLocationPermissionHelper compiled against a controlled CoreLocation adapter returned false and made zero requestAlwaysAuthorization calls for AuthorizedWhenInUse.
- This is a deterministic Kotlin control-flow reproduction, not an iOS runtime test.

## Recommended solution
Model authorizedWhenInUse as eligible for upgrade (not denied/restricted); invoke requestAlwaysAuthorization through a dedicated background state machine with the required usage keys and documented iOS staged/provisional semantics.

## Risks and compatibility

- Test exact callback count and app resume after a settings upgrade.

- [`calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.ios.kt:73-75,106-110`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.ios.kt#L73-L75) — `init/refreshPermissionStatus`
- [`docs/permissions.md:537-544`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/docs/permissions.md#L537-L544) — `Wi-Fi Info.plist example`
- [`sample/ios/Calf/Info.plist:29-30`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/ios/Calf/Info.plist#L29-L30) — `local-network description`

## Root cause
getPermissionStatus constructs/publishes _lnp._tcp. NSNetService and is called while remembering the state, before a user request. A fixed three-second timer, inactive app, publication errors and cancelling an older check all complete false/Denied(true). The required Bonjour service declaration is absent from docs/sample.

## Impact and preconditions
Merely observing permission state can trigger a local-network prompt/advertisement. Slow consent or lifecycle changes look permanently denied; overlapping refreshes can complete a user request falsely. Local-network publication does not establish general Wi-Fi configuration/SSID privileges for all three logical Wi-Fi names.

## Supporting evidence
- init immediately calls refresh -> helper.getPermissionStatus -> publish(); no observational/interactive separation.
- cancel() routes through cleanupAndComplete(false); timeout unconditionally false.
- Docs/sample specify NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription only, not NSBonjourServices.

## Recommended solution
Separate passive status/unknown from explicit user-triggered local-network probing, report timeout/unavailable/cancelled separately, declare NSBonjourServices [_lnp._tcp] and the usage string, serialize probes and clean up on disposal. Document that Wi-Fi access/configuration capabilities are distinct from local-network privacy.

## Risks and compatibility
Apple exposes no universal passive local-network authorization query; do not replace this with another undocumented heuristic presented as authoritative. Whether this exact publish operation prompts on each OS/device needs verification.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Remember state without clicking: no network probe/prompt.
- Consent delayed beyond3s, inactive app, publish error, missing Bonjour declaration, denied and granted on real iOS.
- Concurrent refresh/request, three Wi-Fi aliases, disposal and network unavailable; verify cleanup/no advertisement leakage.

## Dependencies

Route validated updates into public observable state (prefer a single coherent source for simple/extended views), represent no-fix explicitly, remove unused channels or implement a lifecycle-owned consumer, and add regression tests before publishing geo.

The module has no publication plugin and appears to be a prototype. Changing non-null State types requires an additive state/result API or compatibility bridge; do not advertise ready geolocation until verified.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-geo/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/geo/LocationTracker.kt:41-46,111-121`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-geo/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/geo/LocationTracker.kt#L41-L46) — `bind/startTracking/stopTracking`

## Root cause
startTracking is suspend but performs no permission request/check, ignores the returned Google Task and sets isStarted before registering. bind repeats the unchecked request when started. Null/unbound clients silently do nothing; null Looper assumes a suitable caller thread.

## Impact and preconditions
Missing/revoked permissions can throw or fail, unavailable Play Services/settings go unreported, and a successful return does not mean tracking started. A caller using a background coroutine can violate the null-Looper precondition.

## Supporting evidence
- Both registration sites suppress MissingPermission; the comment saying permission failures stop execution has no implementation.
- No await or Task success/failure listener exists in the file.

## Recommended solution
Inject/check permissions explicitly, await/map registration success/failure, require/main-dispatch an explicit Looper, validate bind/start order and expose unavailable/permission/error states. Roll back active state on failure; handle cancellation without leaking an update subscription.

## Risks and compatibility
Permission checks are still subject to TOCTOU revocation, so catch native security failures as well. Introducing automatic background permission escalation would be inappropriate; start should request only documented foreground capabilities.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Denied/revoked/coarse-only permissions, unbound client, no Play Services/location settings off, failed registration/removal Task.
- Start from main/background, cancellation during registration, duplicate starts and recovery after errors.

- **Priority:** High

- [`calf-ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/datepicker/SelectableDays.kt:138-160`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/datepicker/SelectableDays.kt#L138-L160) — `isDaySelectable / snapSelectionToSelectable`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/datepicker/AdaptiveDateRangePicker.ios.kt:50-62,79-82`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/datepicker/AdaptiveDateRangePicker.ios.kt#L50-L62) — `AdaptiveDateRangePicker`

## Root cause
Only the initial iOS single-date value is canonicalized; subsequent assignments are an unvalidated mutableState property. yearRange is stored but is neither validated by the iOS state constructor/setter nor intersected with native bounds or selection predicates. Native single/range callbacks likewise call only isSelectableDate, not isSelectableYear or the state yearRange.

## Impact and preconditions
A public property documented as UTC start-of-day can hold arbitrary intraday values and out-of-range years. Native calendars can offer years that Material-backed state rejects, creating divergent behavior and potentially a callback exception or native/local selection disagreement.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- The iOS constructor advertises IllegalArgumentException at lines30-31 but has no corresponding require.
- selectedDateMillis uses mutableStateOf(canonical initial value) without a custom setter.
- Native applyDateBounds receives only state.dateBounds; both isDaySelectable helpers consult only isSelectableDate, ignoring isSelectableYear and yearRange.

## Recommended solution
Centralize canonicalization and year-range validation for constructor/setters and intersect the effective native selectable range with yearRange. Define programmatic selection versus SelectableDates behavior separately; do not silently add business-rule validation to the Material-compatible setter without an API decision.

## Risks and compatibility
Changing accepted values can affect callers relying on permissive iOS behavior. Native range rejection behavior and exception propagation require Apple execution; the contract/implementation mismatch is source-confirmed, not an observed UIKit crash.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Shared constructor/setter tests for null, intraday UTC, pre-epoch and out-of-range year values.
- iOS inline/wheels/compact/range selection at both year endpoints and outside them.
- Rule changes that would snap outside yearRange; align both actual implementations.
- A rule with isSelectableYear=false but isSelectableDate=true must have an explicit consistent native/Material policy.

## Root cause
UICalendarView and NSDate extraction use NSCalendar.currentCalendar, whereas component year/month/day values are read into or generated from Gregorian kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate without calendar/era conversion.

## Impact and preconditions
Non-Gregorian device calendars can select the wrong year/day or receive nonsensical visible-month data. Buddhist year offsets, Japanese era numbering and leap-month calendars are not interchangeable with Gregorian components; month13 cannot be represented by LocalDate.

- currentCalendar.components(year|month|day) feeds LocalDate(year,month,day) directly.
- calendarView.calendar is explicitly currentCalendar, but outgoing NSDateComponents have Gregorian numbers and no calendar/era.

## Recommended solution
Choose and document the calendar contract. Either configure all UIKit/calendar extraction as Gregorian with the device locale/timezone, or convert through absolute NSDate instants using the originating calendar and era. Use the same policy for visible-month refresh, bounds, callbacks and range highlights.

## Risks and compatibility
This is a source-confirmed incompatible conversion; examples describe mathematical/calendar consequences, not executed iOS outcomes. Retain local-day/DST semantics while fixing calendar identity.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- iPhone/iPad Gregorian, Buddhist, Japanese and Hebrew device calendars.

UIAlertAction handlers and text-field targets are constructed once and capture original immutable action/textField objects. Recomposition replaces iosProperties and updates title/message/enabled by index, but never replaces or redirects callbacks.

## Impact and preconditions
An alert can display newly supplied recordB text while its confirm handler still mutates/deletes recordA. Form edits may reach an obsolete handler. This is more serious than merely stale labels because visible user intent and performed action can differ.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- updateDialogProperties assigns title/message and enabled only.
- toUIAlertAction invokes the onClick captured from its extension receiver; textFieldDidChange captures textFieldState.
- Upstream#519 fix77eeaeb2d249ee559debf82dd2535b4dad733ec8 addressed display updates but not live callbacks.

## Recommended solution
Use latest callback holders addressed by stable action/field identity. Define which structural properties can change during presentation and recreate safely when unsupported structure changes; do not rely solely on list index if actions can reorder.

## Risks and compatibility
Changing action counts during presentation is already documented as unsupported and is not the sole defect. Do not reintroduce the previously fixed weak-target lifetime problem.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Keep alert open, swap title/data/callback fromA toB, then confirm; onlyB callback executes.
- Swap text-field callback without replacing controller, reorder actions safely, change enabled flag.
- Confirm/cancel callback cardinality and full modal lifecycle tests.

## Dependencies

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:UI-014 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** UI-014
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-ui`
- **Estimated complexity:** L
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/dialog/AlertDialogManager.kt:129-184`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/dialog/AlertDialogManager.kt#L129-L184) — `onDismissLambda / dismiss / showAlertDialog`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/dialog/AdaptiveAlertDialog.ios.kt:66-102,118-140`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/dialog/AdaptiveAlertDialog.ios.kt#L66-L102) — `remember / DisposableEffect`

## Root cause
dismiss returns while presentation is animating or not yet marked presented. Disposal calls it once and does not queue cleanup. The manager is remembered by controller but DisposableEffect(Unit) is not. Programmatic cleanup invokes the same onDismissRequest callback as an outside tap, while native action auto-dismissal does not reconcile manager flags.

## Impact and preconditions
Removing an alert before presentation completes can leave an orphaned native modal. Controller changes can retain the wrong effect owner. Duplicate dismissal callbacks and inside-tap interception are additional native risks due to shared cleanup and an unfiltered superview tap recognizer.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- show sets isAnimating=true before isPresented becomes true in completion; dismiss returns when !isPresented||isAnimating.
- onDispose calls dismiss once, and onDismissLambda completion always invokes onDismissRequest.
- Both composables use DisposableEffect(Unit) around a controller-keyed manager.

## Recommended solution
Model requested versus actual presentation state, serialize show/dismiss, and honor pending disposal after presentation completes. Key effects by manager/controller and separate cleanup from user-dismiss notification. Use supported presentation delegates/hit-testing for outside dismissal.

## Risks and compatibility
Dropped early cleanup is source-confirmed. Exact double-callback and tap-recognizer behavior requires native reproduction. Do not re-report the fixed NSObject/unrecognized-selector crash.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Remove composition during presentation and during dismissal; immediately reopen.
- Confirm action followed by caller removal invokes each semantic callback at most once.
- Parent controller replacement, inside text-field taps, outside taps and dismissOnClickOutside=false.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:UI-018 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** UI-018
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-ui`
- **Estimated complexity:** L
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/sheet/SheetState.ios.kt:46-54,61-99`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/sheet/SheetState.ios.kt#L46-L54) — `iosSheetManager / deferredUntilShown / deferredUntilHidden`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/sheet/BottomSheetManager.kt:92-127,133-149`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/sheet/BottomSheetManager.kt#L92-L127) — `show / hide`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/sheet/AdaptiveBottomSheet.ios.kt:104-105,132-145`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/sheet/AdaptiveBottomSheet.ios.kt#L104-L105) — `manager attachment / DisposableEffect`

## Root cause
show/hide return false during animation instead of queueing/awaiting the desired transition. Deferred objects are reset only after a successful await, so cancellation can reuse an already completed deferred. Disposal makes a single hide attempt, immediately forces state Hidden, and never clears the state-to-manager reference; the effect is keyed by Unit rather than its owners.

## Impact and preconditions
Rapid navigation/removal can leave a native sheet displayed after Compose considers it hidden. Later operations may complete before their animations. Hoisted state can retain the presenting controller, sheet controller, content and composition-local context after disposal. Public suspend methods also lack UI-thread confinement.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- deferredUntilShown/Hidden are fields reset after await with no finally.
- hide returns false when !isPresented||isAnimating.
- onDispose ignores hide result and does not set iosSheetManager=null.

## Recommended solution
Use per-operation completion tokens and a serialized, cancellation-safe presentation state machine confined to Main. Ensure disposal records a terminal cleanup request even during animation, detaches only its own manager reference, and releases content/controller ownership when safe.

## Risks and compatibility
Lost hide and stale-deferred paths are source-confirmed. Persistent heap growth and background-thread crashes are risks, not profiled/reproduced facts. Preserve content-local propagation for nested native widgets.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- show then hide before show completes; dispose during either animation.
- Cancel a show/hide waiter, complete native animation, then repeat the operation; await duration must be correct.
- Concurrent callers, owner/state/controller replacement, off-main call policy, weak-reference/heap checks after disposal.

- UI-016
- UI-017

title: [High][UI-027] Liquid Glass slider retains stale enabled, range, geometry and direction inside drag callbacks
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:UI-027 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** UI-027
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-ui`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/slider/LiquidGlassSlider.kt:95-176`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/slider/LiquidGlassSlider.kt#L95-L176) — `dampedDragAnimation / track pointerInput`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/DampedDragAnimation.kt:20-29,66-83`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/DampedDragAnimation.kt#L20-L29) — `DampedDragAnimation.modifier`

## Root cause
DampedDragAnimation is remembered only by animationScope and stores callbacks capturing the initial enabled, valueRange, trackWidth, thumbWidthPx and isLtr. The track pointerInput is keyed only by enabled. didDrag is set after motion but never reset for a new gesture; drag-stop callbacks are not enabled-guarded.

## Impact and preconditions
A slider initially enabled can continue sending thumb-drag changes after it is disabled; initially disabled can stay inert after enabling. Resizing, range replacement or RTL changes can yield wrong values. A later tap can reuse previous drag state.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- remember(animationScope) wraps callbacks using enabled/range/width/direction.
- Only onValueChange and onValueChangeFinished use rememberUpdatedState.
- didDrag has no reset assignment after its initial remember(false).

## Recommended solution
Separate stable gesture machinery from latest parameters via updated-state holders or complete keys; recreate range-bound animation state safely when range changes. Reset gesture-local flags on every start/cancel and consistently gate interactions/completion while disabled.

## Risks and compatibility
This confirms stale capture paths, not an executed iOS input test. Recreating state indiscriminately can interrupt active gestures; define transition/cancellation behavior explicitly.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- enabled true-to-false and false-to-true after first composition, during drag and while idle.
- Resize, density, RTL and valueRange changes without changing enabled.
- Drag then tap, callback replacement, disabled finish/cancel events.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/toggle/LiquidGlassSwitch.kt:145-178,234-235`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/toggle/LiquidGlassSwitch.kt#L145-L178) — `LiquidGlassSwitch semantics / gesture target`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/slider/CupertinoSlider.kt:662-704`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/slider/CupertinoSlider.kt#L662-L704) — `cupertinoSliderSemantics`

## Root cause
The Liquid slider is constructed from Box/pointerInput without range/progress/setProgress/focusable semantics. The Liquid switch sets role/toggleableState/stateDescription but no semantic click/toggle action and only attaches pointer gestures to its40x24dp thumb. It hardcodes English On/Off labels.

## Impact and preconditions
VoiceOver, Switch Control and keyboard users cannot reliably operate these controls through standard semantic actions. This is an accessibility regression from the pre26 Cupertino slider/switch and Material branches, which expose interaction semantics.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- LiquidGlassSlider has no semantics or progressSemantics/focusable call.
- Switch semantics block only assigns role, toggleableState, English stateDescription and disabled.
- CupertinoSlider already uses setProgress/progressSemantics, illustrating the regression.

## Recommended solution
Use foundation toggleable/appropriate slider semantics or equivalent complete actions on the full accessible control, with localized state, disabled/read-only rules, focus and minimum touch targets. Ensure visuals follow the same controlled state as accessibility.

## Risks and compatibility
Missing semantic actions are source-confirmed. Actual iOS assistive-technology traversal and UIKit interop defaults are not tested; do not infer that all native widgets lack accessibility.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- VoiceOver adjust slider/double-tap switch, Switch Control and hardware keyboard on iOS26+.
- Semantics tests for disabled/read-only, min/max/current/steps, localized labels and callback counts.
- Full-track and minimum44pt target checks at large text sizes.

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:UI-031 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** UI-031
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-ui`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/DampedDragAnimation.kt:66-82`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/DampedDragAnimation.kt#L66-L82) — `modifier onDragEnd / onDragCancel`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/DragGestureInspector.kt:21-38,52-58`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/DragGestureInspector.kt#L21-L38) — `inspectDragGestures / drag`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/toggle/LiquidGlassSwitch.kt:103-123`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/toggle/LiquidGlassSwitch.kt#L103-L123) — `onDragStopped`

## Root cause
DampedDragAnimation routes both drag end and cancellation through the same committing onDragStopped callback. The inspector begins immediately on down, without touch slop, and cancels when another recognizer consumes a change; the switch toggles even when didDrag is false.

## Impact and preconditions
A parent scroll recognizer winning the gesture or another pointer cancellation can change application state although the user did not complete a switch activation. Sliders also emit finish/commit callbacks on cancellation.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- onDragCancel calls onDragStopped exactly as onDragEnd does.
- inspectDragGestures calls onDrag with Offset.Zero on first down and returns cancellation when change.isConsumed.

## Recommended solution
Separate cancel from commit in the gesture contract, restore authoritative state on cancellation and arbitrate slop/consumption with standard gesture facilities. Ensure cancellation does not invoke business callbacks.

## Risks and compatibility
The callback-routing defect is source-confirmed; exact nested-scroll/pointer event reproduction requires Compose iOS. Avoid altering normal tap behavior while adding slop handling.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Start on thumb then scroll vertically so parent consumes; no toggle callback.
- Pointer removed/cancelled, second pointer handoff, composable disposal and disabled transition mid-gesture.
- Successful tap/drag each commits exactly once.

## Dependencies
- UI-030

## Classification

- **Priority:** Medium

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/native/.gitignore:1-2`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/native/.gitignore#L1-L2) — `Cargo.lock exclusion`

- [`calf-share/native/Cargo.toml:9-16`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/native/Cargo.toml#L9-L16) — `dependency constraints`

## Root cause
Both cdylib projects ignore Cargo.lock, dependencies use compatible ranges, CI installs dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable and cargo build omits --locked. These are shipped binary inputs, not only source-library development constraints.

## Impact and preconditions
The same Git commit can produce different dependency graphs and binaries over time or from different registry caches. Vulnerability and license inventories cannot be tied reliably to a released native artifact.

## Supporting evidence
- Audit online cargo metadata resolved 197 file-picker packages and 48 share packages including roots
- 202 unique non-root name/version pairs were queried in OSV
- The first offline share resolution and subsequent online picker resolution selected different compatible versions of shared dependencies

## Recommended solution
Commit and maintain both Cargo.lock files, pin rust-toolchain.toml, build with --locked, include locks/toolchain/target in cache keys and retain per-target dependency/license/provenance manifests. Review lock updates rather than suppressing advisories globally.

## Risks and compatibility
A lockfile generated during this audit reflects 2026-10-24 resolution, not the original release graph. Do not present it as the historical shipped graph.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Build one revision from empty caches twice and compare package graphs and reproducibility metadata
- Reject changed dependency resolution under --locked
- Verify CI uses the exact pinned Rust toolchain for every target

- None identified.

## Impact and preconditions
Future builds can execute changed third-party plugin/action/install code or resolve different transitive dependencies. This is a supply-chain risk; the audit found no evidence of a compromised build input.

Maintain Gradle verification metadata and dependency locks, track generated JS package-manager locks with frozen installs, pin actions to reviewed full SHAs, lock Python tooling, and add dependency/license/SBOM review. Keep pull-request workflows read-only and publication credentials in owner-gated protected environments.

## Risks and compatibility
Verification bootstrap must use independently trusted artifacts; auto-accepting every new checksum defeats the control. Locking all KMP target graphs requires cross-platform CI coordination.

- Reject an intentionally modified downloaded build artifact in a local verification fixture
