title: [Medium][BUILD-008] Release version input is embedded directly in executable shell scripts
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:BUILD-008 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** BUILD-008
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `CI`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml:42-46`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml#L42-L46) — `Cargo version stamping`
- [`.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml:102-107`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml#L102-L107) — `Windows version stamping`
- [`.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml:156-160`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml#L156-L160) — `Linux version stamping`
- [`.github/workflows/deploy.yml:121-158`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/.github/workflows/deploy.yml#L121-L158) — `version updates and release branch creation`

## Root cause
workflow_dispatch/workflow_call version strings are interpolated as ${{ inputs.version }} inside shell code before the shell parses it. Quoting the surrounding sed/git command does not make arbitrary GitHub expression text safe.

## Impact and preconditions
A crafted or malformed version may alter shell execution or corrupt manifests. Dispatchers are authenticated repository actors, so this is not an unauthenticated pull-request exploit. Release jobs also expose privileged credentials, increasing the value of a separate release-input boundary.

## Supporting evidence
- Expressions are present literally inside sed double-quoted programs and branch/commit command text at the cited baseline lines
- No malicious workflow input was sent to GitHub during this audit

## Recommended solution
Pass version via an environment variable, validate a narrowly specified version grammar before all use, and use TOML-aware updates or safe arguments rather than string-built shell code. Require explicit owner approval for publication. Migration disables/removes the unsafe release paths; do not restore them unchanged.

## Risks and compatibility
Version grammars must deliberately handle snapshots/prereleases without permitting arbitrary shell/sed metacharacters. Removing old workflows is mitigation, not proof a future release workflow is safe.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria

## Root cause
Android uses nullable stream ?.use chains and unconditionally emits KmpFile(uri) even when opening a stream returned null. iOS ignores NSData.writeToURL Boolean and returns its URL regardless. IO exceptions in remembered coroutine scopes have no common error channel/terminal-result policy.

## Impact and preconditions
Callers may show successful exports for unwritten content, present a picker for nonexistent staging, or remain waiting when failures escape. Partial created documents are not systematically rolled back. A cancellation result cannot communicate a provider/disk failure.

- Android lines 47,52-53 skip failed opens but line 60 still emits a file.
- iOS line 122 ignores the only success result.
- The unmerged PR #551 introduces onError overloads and staging checks; baseline has neither.

## Recommended solution
Check every open/write/copy result, close resources, remove only newly created owned partial files on failure, and add backward-compatible typed onError/result overloads. Keep cancellation distinct and rethrow coroutine cancellation rather than converting it to a generic error.

## Risks and compatibility
Do not delete an existing user-selected destination when cleanup ownership is unknown. Existing callbacks may rely on current null behavior, so document migration semantics.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Resolver returns null input/output stream
- Permission revoked during read/write
- Disk-full and failing close
- iOS writeToURL returns false
- Cancellation during copy
- Exactly one terminal event for success/cancel/error

PHPicker computes processResult with compareAndSet but only gates the empty-result branch; every nonempty didFinishPicking list is processed even when the guard is already set. - Commit e927149 changed the previous unconditional duplicate guard into this branching structure.

## Recommended solution
Use a per-launch terminal-state machine and enforce it for all result branches and late callbacks; support the platform interactive-dismiss callback for document picker and saver as well as photo picker. Keep delegates alive for the session.

## Risks and compatibility
Photo providers may emit cancellation and completion in surprising order; rejecting duplicates must not resurrect the historical lost-result problem. Separate dialog dismissal from asynchronous result-processing completion.

- Two nonempty photo delegate callbacks
- Empty then nonempty callback order
- Swipe dismissal for photo/document/save
- Cancel while NSItemProvider work is running
- Relaunch before old provider callback returns
- No duplicate temp copies/callbacks

## Root cause
Folder selection returns an external NSURL directly and no operation in these modules balances start/stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource or models bookmarks. Android returns SAF/photo URIs without an opt-in persisted grant/bookmark abstraction. Common KmpFile does not express ownership or access expiry.

## Impact and preconditions
External folder/provider access and restored references can fail outside a callback/session or after process restart, despite metadata strings still existing. Nonfolder iOS picks are copied, reducing but not eliminating lifetime concerns for manually wrapped or exported URLs. Exact behavior depends on provider and OS.

- Baseline iOS folder branch uses KmpFile(nsUrl) and forOpeningContentTypes asCopy=false.
- No startAccessingSecurityScopedResource or takePersistableUriPermission call is present in the audited baseline modules.
- PR #551/c70d35c is unmerged prior work on persisted bookmarks; platform consequences here are explicitly risk-classified.

Define explicit ephemeral versus owned versus persisted file handles. Add scoped-access helpers and opt-in bookmark/persistable-permission APIs with release/revocation handling; do not blanket-persist every selection. Document paths that are safe only while access is held.

## Risks and compatibility
Security scopes must be balanced on all exits and must remain active while streaming, not merely while opening. Persisting user permissions is a policy choice and should be explicit. Already sandbox-owned copies must not require successful scope acquisition.

- iCloud/third-party folder access after callback
- Stream open/read/close balances scope
- Android SAF grant release/revoke/restart

- Sandbox-local file path
- Save destination reopened after callback

## Classification

- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-io/src/jsMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.js.kt:11-28`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/jsMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.js.kt#L11-L28) — `readFileAsBytes`
- [`calf-io/src/wasmJsMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.wasmJs.kt:12-34`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/wasmJsMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.wasmJs.kt#L12-L34) — `readFileAsBytes/getResult`
- [`calf-io/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFileSource.web.kt:7-8`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFileSource.web.kt#L7-L8) — `source`

## Root cause
Both implementations use suspendCoroutine, only onloadend, and readyState==DONE as the success test. FileReader reaches DONE on errors/abort too; result can be null. They never inspect error, install onerror/onabort handlers, or abort the reader on coroutine cancellation.

## Impact and preconditions
Read failures can be returned as empty bytes (or fail in interop/callback code) instead of an exception, making corrupt/missing content indistinguishable from a valid empty file. Cancelled screen/request work continues reading and allocating the whole file; source() inherits the behavior.

## Supporting evidence
- Both files branch solely on readyState at their onloadend handler and call continuation.resume.
- FileReader DONE denotes completion rather than successful completion. No error or cancellation branch exists in the source.
- No real-browser FileReader failure was executed in this review.

## Recommended solution
Use a cancellable suspension with exactly-once completion, onload success handling, explicit error/abort propagation, cancellation-triggered FileReader.abort, and listener cleanup. Register handlers before starting the read.

## Risks and compatibility
Abort from cancellation must not cause a second resume. JS and Wasm interop need separate browser tests; a Node typed-array example alone would not prove compiled Kotlin browser behavior.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Readable empty/nonempty files
- FileReader NotReadableError and SecurityError
- Abort before completion and after onload
- Dispose image request during large read
- Exactly one resume and handlers removed
- JS/Wasm parity

## Root cause
Web isDirectory guesses from absence of a dot in file.name, although the representation is a File rather than a directory handle. Common isFile is simply !isDirectory and never establishes existence or a regular-file type.

## Impact and preconditions
A normal browser File named README is called a directory. A missing desktop file has isDirectory=false and therefore isFile=true; device/special-file distinctions are likewise lost. Callers can choose incorrect preview, traversal or validation behavior.

## Supporting evidence
- Web code at line 19 tests only file.name.contains(".").
- The negation at common line 56 evaluates true for desktop java.io.File.isDirectory=false on a missing path.

## Recommended solution
Return false for directories in the current browser File-only abstraction; add a separate directory representation if folder support is introduced. Specify whether isFile means regular existing file or merely not-a-directory, then implement consistent platform queries and compatibility documentation.

## Risks and compatibility
Changing previously permissive isFile semantics is observable. exists is a capability/snapshot question on browser File objects, not a live path probe; do not promise filesystem existence that browsers cannot expose.

## Classification

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.web.kt:21-44,47-60`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.web.kt#L21-L44) — `rememberFileSaverLauncher/triggerDownload`

## Root cause
The web implementation ignores onResult and only clicks a Blob-backed download anchor. The common API has no distinct StartedDownload result or capability indicator, while its callback is documented as saved-file or cancellation.

## Impact and preconditions
Cross-platform UI awaiting completion remains pending on every browser save. A downloaded Blob is not a filesystem-confirmed save, so reporting a made-up KmpFile success would be equally misleading.

## Supporting evidence
- onResult appears only in the function signature in the baseline web saver.
- PR #551/ff62e5b adds a real save path on supporting browsers but still explicitly cannot observe download completion on others.

## Recommended solution
Document and expose download-only versus verifiable-save capabilities. Add a real File System Access API save path where available and a distinct started-download event/fallback contract where completion cannot be observed, keeping old overloads compatible.

## Risks and compatibility
Browser support, secure contexts, user activation and iframe restrictions vary. Do not falsely equate anchor.click with persisted data, or return null cancellation merely because a download was initiated.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Chromium File System Access success/cancel/error if added
- Safari/Firefox download fallback state transition
- Caller never waits for an unsupported terminal event
- User activation and insecure-context fallback
- JS/Wasm parity

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-012 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-012
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.web.kt:51-60`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/FileSaverLauncher.web.kt#L51-L60) — `triggerDownload`

## Root cause
triggerDownload revokes the object URL synchronously immediately after anchor.click and removing the anchor, assuming the browser has already consumed the Blob.

## Impact and preconditions
Browsers that resolve the download after the click returns can see a revoked URL and fail or create no download. This is a source-confirmed lifetime hazard with upstream Safari corroboration, but no Safari/WebKit run was available here.

- Archived unmerged commit 66e345a9b291d4d82aa76b1f5f0d05e99b1bb8e1 describes Safari failures and uses deferred revocation.

## Recommended solution
Retain the URL until a documented safe deferred revocation point or platform-supported completion signal, and clean it up on exceptions. Keep a bounded lifecycle strategy rather than leaking every download URL.

## Risks and compatibility
There is no universal anchor-download completion signal. A delay is a pragmatic fallback, not proof of save completion; large downloads and background tabs must be tested.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Safari macOS and iOS small/large downloads
- Chrome/Firefox unaffected positive paths
- Repeated downloads and URL retention bounds
- Anchor/create/click failure cleanup

title: [Medium][IO-013] iOS picked-file copies have no ownership cleanup and are created before result limits are applied
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-013 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-013
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-io`, `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** L
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.picker/TempFile.kt:13-25`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.picker/TempFile.kt#L13-L25) — `NSURL.createTempFile`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.picker/FilePickerLauncher.ios.kt:105-124`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.picker/FilePickerLauncher.ios.kt#L105-L124) — `document result staging`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.picker/FilePickerLauncher.ios.kt:185-197,266-285`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.picker/FilePickerLauncher.ios.kt#L185-L197) — `photo provider staging`
- [`calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt:15-27`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt#L15-L27) — `KmpFile ownership contract`

## Root cause
Every nonfolder selection creates a new UUID-named file in NSTemporaryDirectory. KmpFile exposes no dispose/release-owned-copy operation and no cleanup registry exists. Document multi-select stages every URL before take(maxItems); cancelled/late photo callbacks can stage files that no caller receives.

## Impact and preconditions
Repeated or very large picks consume unbounded temporary disk until external OS cleanup. Files excluded by maxItems still incur copy IO and survive. The property documentation calls a temp copy persistent even though the OS may purge it.

## Supporting evidence
- TempFile.kt only copies; no complementary delete exists for picker-created copies in these modules. Saver cleanup is a separate list and does not cover picked copies.
- Document list take occurs after mapNotNull and withContext copies at line 122.
- Photo cancellation calls progress.cancel but has no cleanup for copied results abandoned during coroutine delivery.

## Recommended solution
Define owned staging lifetimes and expose explicit release/copy-to-permanent-storage behavior without deleting caller-owned files. Apply limits before staging, remove unreturned copies on cancellation/error, and bound photo provider concurrency. Retain provider temporary content synchronously before the provider callback ends.

## Risks and compatibility
Never delete picked user originals. Automatic early cleanup must not invalidate returned KmpFiles still in use; ownership must be explicit and backwards-compatible. NSItemProvider callback URLs must be copied before callback return.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Repeated pick/release disk accounting
- Select 100 files with maxItems=1 and assert only one staged
- Cancel during provider copy
- Failure halfway through multi-select
- Returned file lifetime and explicit persistence
- OS purge behavior documented

## Dependencies
- IO-007
- IO-008

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-014 -->
## Classification

- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-io`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt:18-24,45-57`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt#L18-L24) — `getName/getPath/isDirectory`
- [`calf-io/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/io/KmpFile.android.kt:40-51`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/io/KmpFile.android.kt#L40-L51) — `getName/getPath/isDirectory`
- [`calf-io/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.web.kt:15-17`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.web.kt#L15-L17) — `getName/getPath`
- [`calf-io/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.kt:26-40`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.kt#L26-L40) — `metadata contract`

## Root cause
iOS extracts a name by splitting originalUrl.absoluteString rather than lastPathComponent, retaining URL escapes. getPath also returns originalUrl.absoluteString rather than the path of its readable temp copy. Android returns URI strings and web returns only names under the same path API.

## Impact and preconditions
Names such as report%20one.pdf are not the expected human/file name; consumers passing getPath to a filesystem API can fail on file:// or content:// strings, inaccessible iOS originals, or ambiguous browser basenames. isDirectory may query a transient original instead of the readable URL.

## Supporting evidence
- iOS names and paths both derive from originalUrl.absoluteString despite the KmpFile docs warning it may be inaccessible.
- Current source() already avoids getPath on Android and uses url.path on iOS; this is the safe content access route.
- PR #551 e2ded9f/b82e19d implements a path-versus-URI distinction; not merged into baseline.

## Recommended solution
Separate URI serialization from optional filesystem paths; define platform guarantees in API docs, use NSURL.lastPathComponent for names and the readable copy for a filesystem path, and encourage source() for content instead of reverse-engineering paths.

## Risks and compatibility
Existing consumers may depend on URI-string getPath behavior. Introduce explicit toUriString/path APIs or a documented migration rather than silently changing all meanings. Preserve original display name when staging.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Space, percent, Unicode and slash-escaped URL names
- Readable iOS temp-copy path after original expires
- Android content:// vs file://
- Two browser files with identical names
- Round-trip URI serialization independent of path

title: [Medium][IO-015] Desktop MIME filtering omits modern image formats and silently disables unknown custom filters
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-015 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-015
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** M

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/platform/PlatformFilePicker.kt:130-144`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/platform/PlatformFilePicker.kt#L130-L144) — `resolveExtensions`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/resources/jodd/net/MimeTypes.properties:651-696`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/resources/jodd/net/MimeTypes.properties#L651-L696) — `image MIME records`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/jodd/net/MimeTypes.kt:133-159`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/jodd/net/MimeTypes.kt#L133-L159) — `findExtensionsByMimeTypes`

## Root cause
Desktop filters translate MIME types through a fixed embedded extension table that has no HEIC, HEIF or AVIF entries. If a requested custom MIME has no extension mapping, resolveExtensions returns null, meaning no filter rather than an unsupported/empty filter.

## Impact and preconditions
Image mode excludes commonly produced image files on Desktop, while Custom(image/avif) unexpectedly permits every file. File-picker filters are UI hints, not security validation; callers must still validate content.

## Supporting evidence
- scripts/audit/io_jvm_probes.py initializes all 981 unique extensions in the unchanged table.
- Probe verifies none of avif/heic/heif occur in image/*, and actual resolveExtensions via a mocked bridge sends null for Custom(image/avif).

## Recommended solution
Update/provenance-pin the MIME data and test contemporary formats. Make unknown MIME behavior explicit and choose a documented fallback/error; preserve the direct Extension path for types the MIME database does not know. Never represent filters as a security boundary.

## Risks and compatibility
Adding extensions does not make every decoder support those formats. Avoid huge wildcard filter overhead and maintain the embedded data license.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- AVIF/HEIC/HEIF present in image filter
- Unknown MIME policy
- Mixed known/unknown custom types
- Extension-only bypass
- Native dialog format acceptance on Linux/Windows/macOS

## Root cause
Desktop picker recreates its native handle for current selectionMode but its once-remembered launch lambda truncates using the initial selectionMode. Desktop saver captures resolvedParentWindow directly in remember without keys/state. iOS photo launcher captures settings directly although only UIViewController keys remember.

## Impact and preconditions
Changing maxItems can enforce the old limit despite current native selection settings. Changing parent window can leave dialogs attached to an old/closed window. Switching Compatible/Current image representation is ignored until launcher recreation.

## Supporting evidence
- Desktop line 167 reads selectionMode from remember { } without currentSelectionMode, unlike currentType/currentOnResult.
- Desktop saver resolvedParentWindow at 27 is captured at 38/55; currentSettings does not update that local capture.
- iOS photo imageRepresentationMode is read from the settings parameter captured inside remember(currentUIViewController).
- Historical c0c2278 improved updated-state handling but did not cover these fields.

## Recommended solution
Use rememberUpdatedState for every changing value read by a retained lambda or make the appropriate values remember keys. Snapshot configuration per launch to avoid applying later settings to in-flight results.

## Risks and compatibility
Recreating a launcher while an external dialog is open must not orphan its session. Parent-handle updates interact with native lifetime ownership.

- Recompose maxItems 2 to 5 and null to limit
- Swap Compose parent window

- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.desktop.kt:166-169`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.desktop.kt#L166-L169) — `result.take(maxItems)`

## Root cause
Multiple(maxItems) has no validation. Negative values reach Kotlin take or native APIs; zero means unlimited in PHPicker but an empty result on truncating platforms. Android PickMultipleVisualMedia has native contract limit constraints, and its own successful/fallback result callback is not post-truncated unlike the explicit OpenMultipleDocuments fallback.

## Impact and preconditions
The same public configuration can throw, select nothing or mean unlimited depending on platform. Small/oversized Android photo limits may be rejected by AndroidX, and OS-controlled fallbacks need consistent enforcement. Device-specific Android behavior was not executed.

## Supporting evidence
- Common Multiple merely stores the nullable Int. iOS uses maxItems directly or 0; truncating implementations call take(maxItems).
- Android lines 146-150 return all media-picker results, unlike explicit document fallback lines 129-131.
- AndroidX exact OS contract behaviors require pinned-version/device tests; no assertion here that every fallback exceeds the limit.

## Recommended solution
Define and validate a portable limit domain (for example null unlimited, positive counts; route count=1 to single selection where required), clamp/adapt to native maximums, and enforce result limits consistently after native fallbacks. Validate at configuration creation rather than deep in callbacks.

## Risks and compatibility
Rejecting values previously accepted on one platform is observable. Keep Multiple companion-object backward compatibility and document Android platform caps for null/unlimited.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- null, -1, 0, 1, 2 and very large limits on each target
- Android native photo picker and ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT fallback
- JS/Wasm negative input does not silently become cancel
- Limit change during composition
- iOS limit0 distinction

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-019 -->
## Classification

- **Affected modules:** `calf-io`, `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** M

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.android.kt:229-251`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.android.kt#L229-L251) — `pickFolder/OpenDocumentTree`
- [`calf-io/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/io/KmpFile.android.kt:12-19,40-51`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/io/KmpFile.android.kt#L12-L19) — `exists/getName/isDirectory`

## Root cause
OpenDocumentTree results retain tree URIs but KmpFile metadata always uses DocumentFile.fromSingleUri, not fromTreeUri or a normalized tree document URI. exists attempts to open an InputStream, which is a content-readability operation rather than a directory existence test.

## Impact and preconditions
A successfully picked directory can be reported nonexistent, unnamed or not a directory on providers that do not support opening a tree URI as a stream or querying it as a single document. Exact provider behavior varies, so this finding is not labeled an instrumented Android failure.

## Supporting evidence
- Folder callback at 241 returns KmpFile(uri) unchanged.
- All metadata routes in KmpFile.android.kt use fromSingleUri; exists only tests openInputStream.

## Recommended solution
Recognize tree/document/file URI forms, use tree-aware metadata and existence queries, and separate directory capabilities from byte-stream capabilities. Preserve the original URI/grant for child enumeration.

## Risks and compatibility
DocumentFile.fromSingleUri accepts URIs without validating their semantic kind, so its construction alone does not prove a provider query succeeds. Provider exceptions and revoked grants need explicit handling.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- ExternalStorageProvider, Downloads and cloud-provider folder URIs
- Folder exists/name/isDirectory immediately and after restart
- Single-document and file:// regression tests
- Permission denial and unavailable provider

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-020 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-020
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-io`, `calf-file-picker-coil`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-io/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/io/KmpFile.android.kt:30-37`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/io/KmpFile.android.kt#L30-L37) — `KmpFile.readByteArray`

## Root cause
inputStream.close runs in also after readBytes returns successfully; no use/finally surrounds the read. A provider read exception bypasses closure.

## Impact and preconditions
Failing cloud/provider streams can retain file descriptors and remote provider resources. Repeated image loads through KmpFileFetcher can accumulate leaked resources.

## Supporting evidence
- readBytes().also { inputStream.close() } at lines 35-37 has no exceptional cleanup.
- The streaming source() returns an owned RawSource with explicit caller-close documentation; this finding targets readByteArray, not that ownership contract.

## Recommended solution
Wrap openInputStream in use and return the read from inside it, preserving primary exceptions and ensuring the stream closes on read/close failure. Prefer streaming where consumers support it.

## Risks and compatibility
Closure must occur exactly once and preserve read exceptions with suppressed close failures. Cancellation alone does not interrupt every blocking InputStream.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- InputStream throws after partial bytes and close count is one
- Successful and empty reads close once
- close itself throws
- Null resolver stream still reports not found
- Coil failed-fetch path

title: [Medium][IO-021] Coil fetches eagerly copy whole files and the byte-array API needs explicit scheduling/size guidance
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-021 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-021
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `improvement` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker-coil`, `calf-io`
- **Estimated complexity:** L
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker-coil/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/coil/KmpFileFetcher.kt:22-32`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker-coil/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/coil/KmpFileFetcher.kt#L22-L32) — `fetch`
- [`calf-io/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/io/KmpFile.desktop.kt:12`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/io/KmpFile.desktop.kt#L12) — `readByteArray`
- [`calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt:35-41`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt#L35-L41) — `readByteArray`
- [`calf-io/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFileSource.web.kt:7-8`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFileSource.web.kt#L7-L8) — `eager web source`
- [`calf-io/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.kt:18-24,73-82`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.kt#L18-L24) — `readByteArray docs`

## Root cause
Fetcher always materializes a ByteArray then copies it into an Okio Buffer before decoding, despite native streaming IO now being available. readByteArray is suspend but performs blocking IO on Android/iOS/Desktop without dispatcher switching. Web source is intentionally buffered; iOS also materializes NSData before ByteArray.

## Impact and preconditions
Large media produce multiple encoded-data copies plus decoder allocations, increasing latency and OOM pressure. UI callers may assume suspend means nonblocking even though source() alone documents dispatcher ownership. MEMORY labeling and lack of a supplied stable KmpFile cache key also merit integration tests.

## Supporting evidence
- Fetcher lines 25-26 allocate through readByteArray and then Buffer.write.
- source() implementation and docs explicitly provide native streaming while web remains whole-buffer.
- No heap benchmark or complete Coil runtime test was run, so this is an improvement with quantified benchmarks required, not a measured regression.

## Recommended solution
Add native streaming adapters/URI or file mappers to Coil (or the official kotlinx-io/Okio bridge) with correct close/cancellation ownership; keep a bounded browser fallback. Document readByteArray blocking/size semantics, add decode-size guidance, and verify dataSource/keying behavior with Coil rather than inferring it.

## Risks and compatibility
Changing fetchers may affect EXIF, seek requirements, caching and thread selection. Do not label intended read-all behavior a security vulnerability; source() is already available for large-file consumers.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Large image peak-memory benchmark by target
- Decoder failure closes source
- Coil cancellation closes provider stream
- Stable request key and modified-file invalidation policy
- Main-thread misuse guidance test/sample
- Binary content parity

- IO-001
- IO-020

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-023 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-023
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** L
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/platform/PlatformFilePicker.kt:24-38,46-54,62-74`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/platform/PlatformFilePicker.kt#L24-L38) — `parentWindow.windowHandle acquisition`
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.desktop.kt:116-130`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/picker/FilePickerLauncher.desktop.kt#L116-L130) — `IO-thread handle creation`
- [`calf-file-picker/native/src/lib.rs:105-128,139-162,179-187,218,246-247`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/native/src/lib.rs#L105-L128) — `ParentWindow/unsafe Send+Sync/build`

## Root cause
Rust stores raw window/display handles for reuse and unsafely asserts Send/Sync. macOS temporarily retains NSWindow and contentView during construction, then drops those Retained objects while storing only a raw NSView pointer. Creation can occur on Dispatchers.IO, including the AppKit contentView call and AWT/Compose handle retrieval. Lifetime comments are not enforced by ownership.

## Impact and preconditions
Window close/replacement or off-thread native access can yield stale handles or thread-affinity failures on affected platforms. Linux fabricates an Xlib handle/display hint and cannot represent all Wayland parents. No macOS/Windows/native-GUI failure was executed in Linux.

## Supporting evidence
- ParentWindow safety comments say the JVM AWT thread supplies a handle, but Kotlin constructs picker configs in Dispatchers.IO.
- macOS Retained values are local to from_raw_ptr; DialogConfig retains only ParentWindow raw fields.
- These are code-level precondition gaps; actual UI/backend behavior remains unverified.

## Recommended solution
Acquire platform handles on their required UI thread, retain owning native objects for the complete dialog session where needed, validate the supported Linux backend/handle kind, and release safely when dialogs/window sessions finish. Document unsupported ownership/modality combinations.

## Risks and compatibility
raw-window-handle borrowed lifetimes cannot be satisfied by comments alone. Main-thread dispatch must avoid deadlocks with rfd internal dispatch and Kotlin synchronous JNI calls.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- macOS main-thread checker during create/show/dispose
- Close/recreate parent while dialog opens
- Windows owned-dialog focus and parent destruction
- Linux X11 and Wayland portal parenting
- No-parent supported fallback

title: [Medium][IO-024] JNI path conversion silently replaces non-Unicode filenames
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-024 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-024
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-file-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/native/src/lib.rs:39-68`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/native/src/lib.rs#L39-L68) — `paths_to_jstring_array/path_to_jstring`

## Root cause
Native paths not representable as Rust UTF-8 strings are converted with to_string_lossy and returned as ordinary Java paths. The original byte sequence is not preserved and no conversion error is reported.

## Impact and preconditions
On Unix filesystems with non-UTF-8 filenames, a chosen file can become an unopenable path or potentially refer to a distinct existing replacement-character name. Directory/save paths have the same lossy conversion. Public String/File APIs limit portable recovery.

## Supporting evidence
- Both helper fallbacks explicitly call to_string_lossy().into_owned().
- No real native file-picker selection of an invalid-UTF-8 name was run; the irreversible conversion is source-confirmed.

## Recommended solution
Define supported filename encoding explicitly; reject nonrepresentable paths with a typed error instead of silently substituting, or introduce an opaque/native path representation if preserving arbitrary Unix names is required.

## Risks and compatibility
JNI modified UTF-8 conversion and valid Unicode supplementary characters are a separate concern: jni crate handles ordinary Java/Rust strings. Do not claim all Unicode names are broken.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Unix raw invalid-UTF-8 filename fixture
- Distinct replacement-character filename beside invalid-byte file
- Normal non-ASCII/emoji filenames

## Root cause
FilePickerFileType.Document carries application/*, but the iOS mapping converts it to UTTypeApplication, which describes application bundles rather than the MIME application category containing PDFs, Office documents, archives and other data.

Define the intended Document set and map to explicit document UTTypes or a broad appropriate data/content type; do not equate MIME top-level categories with similarly named UTI constants. Retain specific Pdf/Word/Spreadsheet paths.

## Risks and compatibility
A broad UTTypeData fallback may include more than application/*; document the platform difference or supply a curated type list. Unknown Custom MIME types also need a deliberate empty-list fallback/error policy.

The broad try/catch includes currentOnResult; if application code throws after receiving selected files the catch calls onResult again with an empty list. oncancel invokes the callback before cleanup without finally. Inputs are per-launch DOM nodes with no DisposableEffect/session owner, and fileDialogVisible is never set true or used as a launch guard.

## Impact and preconditions
A callback exception can become a misleading second cancellation event; a throwing cancel handler leaves the node attached. Disposal while the dialog is open can retain callbacks/DOM nodes and later update an obsolete screen, while repeated launch calls have no explicit concurrency policy.

## Supporting evidence
- JS line 75 callback is inside try, catch line 78 invokes callback again; Wasm lines 72/75 mirror it.
- oncancel cleanup follows callback without finally; no DisposableEffect exists in either source file.
- No browser/UI lifecycle execution was available; branch/error behavior is source-confirmed.

## Recommended solution
Separate selection conversion failures from user callback invocation, put cleanup in finally before delivering terminal events, and own DOM/listener lifetime per launch/composition. Add an exactly-once completion guard and a supported repeated-launch policy.

## Risks and compatibility
Browser cancel-event support and user-activation timing vary. Do not swallow fatal/application errors as user cancellation or remove a node so early that native events are lost on a supported browser.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- onResult throws after success: no second callback
- oncancel throws: node still removed
- Composition disposed during dialog
- Two launch attempts
- Same file reselect and normal cancellation
- JS/Wasm parity

- [`calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt:208-247,345-383`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt#L208-L247) — `WKNavigationDelegate and KVO`
- [`calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt:50-65,76-95,183-228`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt#L50-L65) — `content/navigation loaders and iframe listeners`

## Root cause
Desktop RUNNING does not clear errorsForCurrentRequest. iOS clears errors only at didCommitNavigation, so consecutive provisional failures accumulate old errors. Web never sets Loading when changing src/srcdoc and never clears prior errors/title; its cross-origin load handler cannot read URL/title and leaves old values. Web navigation capability flags are unconditionally false.

## Impact and preconditions
A successful retry can retain an old error, a new request can appear Finished, and cross-origin content may display a previous page title/URL. Consumers deriving loading/error/security UI from common state receive inconsistent or stale signals.

## Supporting evidence
- Android onPageStarted resets errors/title, providing the existing comparison behavior.
- Desktop writes errors only on FAILED; iOS reset is didCommit only; Web event source has no Loading assignment anywhere.

## Recommended solution
Centralize begin-request state reset and terminal-state handling; separate requested URL from observable final URL; explicitly represent unknown cross-origin title/history. Clear errors at provisional request start on iOS and RUNNING on Desktop. Do not infer iframe load success from the load event alone.

## Risks and compatibility
Browser deliberately hides many iframe errors and cross-origin metadata; do not promise reliable progress/final URL or bypass same-origin policy. History capability may need an explicit unsupported state rather than invented booleans.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Fail→success, fail→fail, reload, stop and redirects on every target.
- Browser same-origin→cross-origin→inline transitions; blocked framing and offline destination.
- iOS provisional DNS/TLS failure before commit resets the previous request errors.

Separate persistent desired content from one-shot commands, or add an explicit owner/acknowledgement strategy. Choose and document what happens to commands sent before attachment rather than replacing replay=1 blindly.

## Risks and compatibility
Changing to replay=0 without buffering breaks pre-attachment loadUrl/loadHtml calls, including saveable-state patterns. Preserve these intentionally with tests.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Consume Back then replace collector; second collector must not repeat it.

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-009 -->
## Classification

- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt:83-92,111-124,251-258`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt#L83-L92) — `URL load, factory and applySettings`
- [`calf-webview/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebSettings.kt:140-146`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebSettings.kt#L140-L146) — `IosSettings.allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures`

## Root cause
Factory first assigns allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures=captureBackPresses, then applySettings assigns the independent setting whose default is true. Every state-driven URL load also unconditionally sets the property true.

## Impact and preconditions
Disabling captureBackPresses cannot reliably disable swipe navigation; setting the iOS flag false is undone by subsequent URL content changes. Applications with sensitive/special back navigation may unexpectedly leave a page.

## Supporting evidence
- Default true settings overwrite captureBackPresses at factory time; line91 forces true again.

## Recommended solution
Define precedence (for example captureBackPresses AND the iOS option), apply it from a single update path, and remove the unconditional URL-load assignment. Observe captureBackPresses changes on recomposition.

## Risks and compatibility
Fixing precedence changes behavior for consumers accidentally relying on the override; document the intended combined contract.

title: [Medium][NATIVE-011] Browser CookieManager silently misrepresents URL, expiry, HttpOnly and deletion support
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-011 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-011
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.web.kt:12-45`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.web.kt#L12-L45) — `setCookie/getCookies/removeAllCookies`
- [`calf-webview/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/Cookie.kt:10-22`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/Cookie.kt#L10-L22) — `Cookie contract`

## Root cause
Web setters append numeric epoch milliseconds directly as expires, whereas cookies require an HTTP date. URL parameters are ignored in favor of host document.cookie. JavaScript cannot set HttpOnly; the implementation appends that attribute anyway. Deletion always uses path=/ and has no original domain/path.

## Impact and preconditions
An already-expired cookie can become a session cookie, requested HttpOnly writes can be rejected, cross-origin URL queries return host cookies, and logout-style removeAllCookies leaves non-root-path/domain/HttpOnly cookies. Callers receive Unit/normal lists rather than capability/error information.

## Supporting evidence
- Chrome153: invalidExpiresRetainsExpiredCookie=true; httpOnlyAttemptRejected=true; rootOnlyDeletionLeavesPathCookie=true.
- Both url parameters are unused. Common CookieManager documentation still says Web is no-op, while source actively writes host cookies.

## Recommended solution
Format expiry as UTC HTTP date or valid Max-Age; reject unsupported foreign-origin/HttpOnly operations explicitly; scope browser cookie APIs to the actual document context; document that complete domain/path/HttpOnly clearing requires server cooperation and/or tracked cookie identities.

## Risks and compatibility
Chrome rejected the entire HttpOnly assignment; do not claim it created an insecure non-HttpOnly cookie. Browsers may vary. Reading HttpOnly cookies via JavaScript is intentionally impossible and must not be bypassed.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Past/future expiry and session cookies in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit.
- Verify HttpOnly requests surface unsupported status rather than silent success.
- URL mismatch, path-specific/domain cookies and server-set HttpOnly logout cases.
- Cookie names/values containing delimiters are validated rather than changing attributes.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

title: [Medium][NATIVE-012] Desktop and iOS getCookies do not implement full request-URL cookie matching

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-012 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-012
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.desktop.kt:42-57`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.desktop.kt#L42-L57) — `getCookies`
- [`calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.ios.kt:75-103`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.ios.kt#L75-L103) — `getCookies domain-only filtering`

## Root cause
Desktop returns CookieStore.get(uri), which does not apply request-path matching performed by CookieManager.get. iOS fetches all cookies and filters only on host/domain suffix, ignoring path and secure scheme, and cannot express host-only scope in the public Cookie model.

## Impact and preconditions
Returned cookies may not be applicable to the requested URL. Callers copying results into request headers can leak a path-restricted token or, on iOS, a Secure cookie into a non-HTTPS request. This API does not itself send the cookie or alter WebKit request filtering.

## Supporting evidence
- Actual Desktop CookieManager standalone probe returned a cookie restricted to /private for https://audit.invalid/public/.
- iOS filter at86-92 uses only host/domain; no scheme/path predicates occur.

## Recommended solution
Specify whether the method lists storage metadata or cookies applicable to a request. If request matching is intended, implement RFC6265 host-only/domain/path/secure/expiry rules or use the native request-cookie API; otherwise rename/add a scoped method and document restrictions.

## Risks and compatibility
Desktop path mismatch was executed; iOS matching was source-reviewed only. Native browser cookie enforcement itself is not shown to be broken. Cookie path is not a general same-origin security boundary, but callers still must not forward inappropriate credentials.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Domain exact/subdomain/host-only, /private versus /public, /foo versus /foobar paths.
- Secure cookie queried over HTTP versus HTTPS and expiry boundary.
- Compare returned set with actual native HTTP request headers, including duplicate names on different paths.

## Dependencies

title: [Medium][NATIVE-014] Desktop cookie expiry is recalculated from read time and drifts into the future
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-014 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-014
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.desktop.kt:30-37,50-54`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/CookieManager.desktop.kt#L30-L37) — `setCookie/getCookies expiresDate mapping`

## Root cause
HttpCookie.maxAge is a lifetime measured from creation, not remaining time. getCookies converts it to epoch expiry using current time on every read rather than preserving the creation timestamp/original expiry.

## Impact and preconditions
Repeated reads report later and later expiration while the Java cookie store still expires at the original time. Code persisting or copying those returned cookies can extend sessions unintentionally and show misleading session lifetime.

## Supporting evidence
- Actual Desktop CookieManager probe reported +1201ms expiry drift after ~1.2s without rewriting the cookie.

## Recommended solution
Preserve an absolute expiry in controlled metadata or use a backend exposing creation/expiry; otherwise explicitly mark expiry unavailable rather than inventing it. Keep session/maxAge=0 distinctions.

## Risks and compatibility
The store itself still expires cookies; this finding concerns exposed metadata and downstream copying. Avoid relying on inaccessible JDK internals to read creation time.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Set a cookie with a known future expiry; reads separated in time remain at the same absolute expiry.
- Roundtrip returned cookie to another store without increasing lifetime.
- Session, already-expired, near-second-boundary and overflow-sized timestamps.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-015 -->
## Classification

- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/web/WebView.android.kt:375-378`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/web/WebView.android.kt#L375-L378) — `evaluateJavascript`
- [`calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt:188-195`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt#L188-L195) — `evaluateJavascript`
- [`calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.desktop.kt:204-208`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.desktop.kt#L204-L208) — `evaluateJavascript`
- [`calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt:152-159`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt#L152-L159) — `evaluateJavascript`

## Root cause
Android/iOS call native APIs on the caller thread and silently omit callback when no view exists. Desktop queues to FX but does not catch executeScript exceptions. iOS sends localized error text through the same String channel as success. Android returns native JSON-encoded values while other targets use toString; Web catches errors as null.

## Impact and preconditions
Portable client code cannot reliably distinguish null, error text, quoted string and successful string, and may wait forever for callbacks or cause UI-thread violations/uncaught FX exceptions. A callback throwing inside the Web try block can itself trigger a second callback(null).

## Supporting evidence
- Source methods differ in both dispatch and error handling; no common result normalization exists.
- The Android JavascriptInterface annotation does not itself register a JS bridge; no addJavascriptInterface call exists in the module.

## Recommended solution
Add a typed result/error API with documented serialization and exactly-once callback/suspend semantics; route native execution to the correct UI dispatcher, handle absent/disposed views and script errors explicitly. Preserve the old function as a documented compatibility adapter.

## Risks and compatibility
Do not expose a universal unsafe bridge to untrusted pages while adding functionality. Existing consumers may depend on Android JSON encoding; changes need additive compatibility treatment.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Evaluate string, number, object, null, undefined and throwing scripts on all targets.
- Call before attach, after dispose, off main thread and after callback substitution.
- Callback exceptions are not misreported as script failures or delivered twice.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

- [`calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt:94-100,272-289`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt#L94-L100) — `HTML data loaders`
- [`calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt:50-59,220-226`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt#L50-L59) — `iframe loads`

## Root cause
Desktop drops additionalHttpHeaders, baseUrl, encoding and historyUrl. Web drops URL headers and HTML base/mime/encoding/history entirely. iOS state-driven HTML only calls loadHTMLString, while navigator HTML with a base URL encodes bytes as UTF8 regardless of the requested encoding label. Common documentation claims headers apply to all subsequent requests although mobile code only sets them on the requested load.

## Impact and preconditions
Authentication/header-dependent pages or relative HTML resources can fail silently; iOS non-UTF8 labels can mismatch UTF8 data. Applications cannot infer parity from the common signatures. Automatic forwarding of credential headers would itself need an origin policy.

## Supporting evidence
- Desktop engine.load receives only content.url/event.url. Web assigns only src/srcdoc.
- iOS navigator line275 always dataUsingEncoding(NSUTF8StringEncoding), but line282 uses caller event.encoding.

## Recommended solution
Document and expose capability restrictions; validate/reject unsupported options rather than implying support. Share consistent state/navigator loaders. If implementing headers/base URLs, do not leak authorization across origins; encode bytes consistently with the declared encoding.

## Risks and compatibility
Browser cannot attach arbitrary headers to iframe navigation; a proxy/fetch workaround changes origin, cookies, CSP and security and is not a routine fix. Do not promise full web/native parity.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Authenticated URL with custom header, redirect to same/different origin and subsequent links/subresources.
- Inline relative URLs with baseUrl and non-ASCII data under supported encodings.
- State versus navigator content produce the same semantics per platform.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

The factory constructs WKWebView() with default configuration, then sets configuration.allowsInlineMediaPlayback. Apple’s configuration property returns a copy and changing that configuration does not affect the existing web view. Dynamic changes repeat the same ineffective scalar assignment.

The common default/setting can report inline playback enabled while iPhone behavior remains the native default. Consumers cannot reliably opt into inline playback using the exposed API.

Create WKWebViewConfiguration before native view initialization and pass it to WKWebView(frame, configuration). Clearly separate creation-only options from mutable preferences; recreate deliberately or reject unsupported runtime changes.

No iOS playback run was possible. Evidence concerns the scalar configuration field, not an assumption that every nested preferences property is copied or that all JavaScript toggles fail.

## Classification

- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** M

## Exact code / symbols

## Root cause
JFXPanel() is created synchronously inside remember. The first panel can bootstrap JavaFX and enter a nested AWT event loop while Compose is composing/rendering; archived issue346 shows exactly this stack path. There is no coordinated preinitialization or failure UI.

## Impact and preconditions
On affected runtime/host combinations first WebView composition may re-enter Compose rendering and throw Reentry into ignoringRedrawRequests. Missing graphics/native prerequisites can also abort toolkit startup, but their exact root causes differ.

- Archived issue346 stack includes SwingInteropContainer reentry via JFXPanel.initFx and library WebView creation.
- Current source retains direct remember { JFXPanel() }. Issue344 setting-thread failure is different and has a source fix (Platform.runLater at215-221).

## Recommended solution
Reproduce on current supported hosts/Compose first. Establish a documented toolkit startup stage outside an active composition and an error/capability path; marshal UI objects to their required threads and preserve multiwindow lifecycle.

## Risks and compatibility
Historical stack is evidence of a reported prior failure, not proof that current Compose1.12 reproduces it. JavaFX19 classifiers/prerequisites are separately tracked by build findings. Do not blindly move JFXPanel construction to a worker thread.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Cold first WebView creation during recomposition with FX initially uninitialized.

title: [Medium][NATIVE-020] Camera callback/lifetime handling is unstable across recomposition
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-020 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-020
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-camera-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-camera-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.android.kt:22-25,59-73`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-camera-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.android.kt#L22-L25) — `CameraPickerLauncherAndroidImpl and remember factory`
- [`calf-camera-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.ios.kt:29-30,100-105`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-camera-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.ios.kt#L29-L30) — `pickerDelegate and remember(viewController,onResult)`

## Root cause
Android remember has no keys and permanently captures the first onResult/context. iOS keys the whole launcher on onResult, so replacing an inline callback replaces the object that owns the strong UIImagePicker delegate reference during an in-flight operation.

## Impact and preconditions
Android can call a stale handler capturing an obsolete item/navigation identity. iOS has a conditional delegate-lifetime risk when old launcher ownership is lost on recomposition; the existing strong-reference fix is only effective while that launcher remains retained.

## Supporting evidence
- Android launcher construction closes over onResult only once at70.
- iOS remember(viewController,onResult) creates a new launcher for changed function identity; UIKit delegate is weak.

## Recommended solution
Remember one launcher per platform host, keep onResult current via rememberUpdatedState, and explicitly retain/clear active operation delegates independent of changing callbacks. Define which callback receives an in-flight request result.

## Risks and compatibility
Android stale capture is source-confirmed. Premature iOS deallocation under Kotlin/Native GC is a risk, not reproduced; do not undo the original strong delegate retention from PR326.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Change callback from A to B while capture is active and assert agreed callback semantics.
- Repeated ordinary recompositions do not replace iOS active operation owner.
- Force Kotlin/Native GC/memory pressure during presentation and verify delegate callbacks still arrive.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

The sample provider is exported=false with temporary grants: whole-cache path is not proof all cache files are publicly readable. Treat narrowing as defense in depth, not an existing unauthenticated data leak.

title: [Medium][NATIVE-023] iOS camera has no in-flight presentation guard or lifecycle-bound cleanup

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-023 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-023
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-camera-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-camera-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.ios.kt:29-32,49-95`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-camera-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.ios.kt#L29-L32) — `launch, delegate storage and presentation`

## Root cause
Each launch replaces the single pickerDelegate field and schedules another presentation without checking an already-presented controller or active request. Delegate completion calls onResult before dismissal/clearing; a reentrant launch or throwing callback can skip cleanup or overwrite the new operation delegate. Composition disposal is not handled.

## Impact and preconditions
Rapid/reentrant launch can cause UIKit presentation rejection, lost/weak delegates or results; leaving the screen can leave a controller/work active. A throwing callback can leave the original picker undismissed. These cases are not safely serialized.

## Supporting evidence
- launch unconditionally overwrites pickerDelegate at88; completion invokes onResult at64 then clears shared field at70.
- No DisposableEffect/close/in-flight flag exists in the iOS launcher.

## Recommended solution
Represent an explicit active request with a single-flight guard and stable owner, dismiss/clear in finally using instance identity, and define cancellation on owner disposal. Deliver user callbacks after internal lifecycle cleanup when appropriate.

## Risks and compatibility
UIKit/device timing and GC outcomes were not reproduced. The source shows missing guards/order, not guaranteed crash for every double tap. Coordinate callback ownership with NATIVE-020.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Double tap launch, callback launches again, callback throws, owner navigates away.
- Denied permissions, camera unavailable, simulator fallback and presentation over another modal.
- Exactly one active picker and no old delegate cleanup clears a replacement operation.

## Dependencies
- NATIVE-020

title: [Medium][NATIVE-024] Camera capture does synchronous full-resolution PNG work and has no temporary-file ownership policy
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-024 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-024
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-camera-picker`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-camera-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.ios.kt:57-83`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-camera-picker/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.ios.kt#L57-L83) — `UIImagePNGRepresentation and saveTempImageFile`
- [`calf-camera-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.android.kt:35-49`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-camera-picker/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/camerapicker/CameraPickerLauncher.android.kt#L35-L49) — `cache output and handleResult`

## Root cause
The iOS delegate synchronously encodes the original full-resolution UIImage as PNG and atomically writes the whole NSData before dismissing/calling success. iOS random-named and Android timestamp-named temporary files have no cleanup/ownership contract; cancelled/abandoned Android captures are not deleted.

## Impact and preconditions
Large photos can stall the main thread and temporarily retain decoded image plus PNG buffer plus file-write resources. Repeated captures can accumulate sensitive photos/cache space until external cleanup; callers do not know when returned files may disappear.

## Supporting evidence
- UIImagePNGRepresentation, NSData writeToFile and callback all execute inside the UIKit result delegate synchronously.
- Neither platform has a delete/close/TTL path for capture outputs.

## Recommended solution
Measure representative large images, move safe encoding/file work off the UI thread, offer bounded format/quality/resolution policy, and define explicit ownership/TTL for returned files. Delete only failed/cancelled library-owned outputs; successful files must remain valid for documented consumption.

## Risks and compatibility
Latency/OOM/disk growth magnitude is workload/device-dependent and was not benchmarked. Temporary directories are OS-managed but not immediate guaranteed cleanup. JPEG/HEIF choices affect transparency, quality, orientation and metadata.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Real-device 12/48MP capture latency, peak resident memory and UI responsiveness.
- Disk-full/write-failure/cancel/repeated capture and cache eviction.
- File remains readable for expected consumer lifetime; cleanup never deletes another request file.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/pull/311
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/pull/326

Make result semantics explicit per platform and distinguish Presented/Selected from Completed where native APIs permit. Android cannot generally prove a recipient delivered content; macOS should observe the service delegate for actual completion if claiming it. Preserve existing API through a documented additive result model.

## Risks and compatibility
Do not promise actual delivery through share targets that expose no completion API. A compatibility change to Success meaning requires migration notes. Files must remain available while the recipient/service still reads them.

## Root cause
copyToClipboard discards navigator.clipboard.writeText Promise and returns Unit. The caller immediately reports Success in a synchronous try/catch; asynchronous permission/insecure-context rejections bypass that catch and have no rejection handler.

Unsupported native sharing can falsely report a successful copy while nothing reaches the clipboard and an unhandled rejection is emitted. The user loses a fallback action without useful feedback.

Return/await clipboard completion via callback/promise/suspend interop and map rejection to a real unavailable/failure outcome. Check secure context/API support and preserve user activation requirements.

## Risks and compatibility
The Node proof uses the exact Wasm JS body with a mocked rejection, not real clipboard permission UI. Browser integration must test both JS/Wasm and real activation. Never read unrelated clipboard contents in tests.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Rejected NotAllowedError promise produces no Success and no unhandled rejection.
- Resolved promise produces one Success only after completion.

Require/validate content URIs or convert library-owned local files through an explicitly configured FileProvider before launching. Preserve document-provider URI grants and avoid granting write/all-cache access unnecessarily; surface meaningful failure.

## Risks and compatibility
The API also correctly supports content:// KmpFiles. Do not blanket-copy arbitrary provider files or broaden grants merely to support file://. Device intent behavior still requires instrumented validation.

- Internal File.toKmpFile on API24+ produces a recipient-readable content URI.
