title: [Medium][NATIVE-029] macOS share leaks both the Objective-C delegate and its Arc completion state on every presented picker
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-029 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-029
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-share`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-share/native/src/lib.rs:148-162,255-259,294-295`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/native/src/lib.rs#L148-L162) — `did_choose, Arc::into_raw and mem::forget(delegate)`

## Root cause
A cloned Arc is converted into a raw pointer in the delegate ivar, but no dealloc or completion cleanup ever consumes that owning raw reference. did_choose reconstructs it and immediately forgets it. The Objective-C delegate itself is mem::forget-ed permanently with no owner to release it.

## Impact and preconditions
Each picker that reaches delegate creation leaks a native object and its Rust mutex/condition-variable allocation, including dismissal and timeout. The source leak is definite, while the per-request memory size is not measured.

## Supporting evidence
- Arc::into_raw(ctx.pair.clone()) increments ownership at256; no matching owning drop exists.
- std::mem::forget(delegate) at295 has no later Retained::from_raw/release counterpart.

## Recommended solution
Use an explicit retained operation owner and balanced lifetime/teardown. Release the raw Arc exactly once from delegate dealloc or a safely synchronized completion path, clear the pointer, and release delegate/picker after callbacks can no longer occur. Handle late callbacks after timeout without use-after-free.

## Risks and compatibility
Naively dropping the delegate immediately or Arc after the waiting thread wakes risks a weak-delegate loss or use-after-free. ObjC callback lifetime, picker retention and duplicate callbacks require a real macOS design/test, not a one-line mem::forget removal.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Thousands of share/cancel cycles show stable allocations under Instruments/leaks.
- Success, cancellation, timeout, no-window and late/duplicate callbacks drop each owner exactly once.
- ASan/native stress with concurrent requests validates no UAF or double-free after cleanup.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-share/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/ShareLauncher.desktop.kt:24-35,74-85`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/ShareLauncher.desktop.kt#L24-L35) — `rememberShareLauncher/showNativeShare`

## Root cause
The JNI function schedules AppKit work then synchronously waits on Condvar with a 300-second timeout. withContext(Dispatchers.IO) does not make this native blocking call cancellable. There is no native cancellation handle or single-flight request guard; spurious wakes restart a full timeout window.

## Impact and preconditions
Leaving composition cancels the coroutine result delivery but cannot close the picker or immediately release the worker. Repeated launches can occupy many workers and show overlapping native UI. Missing/late callbacks turn into Dismissed after a long delay unrelated to actual user dismissal.

## Supporting evidence
- Rust uses Duration::from_secs(300) and wait_timeout in a loop; Kotlin wraps it only with Dispatchers.IO.

## Recommended solution
Expose asynchronous native completion or a cancellable operation handle, serialize appropriate UI requests, and use an absolute deadline with a distinct timeout/error outcome. Keep all AppKit calls on main and ensure completion-state lifetime handles cancellation/late callbacks.

## Risks and compatibility
The existing implementation correctly keeps the blocking wait off the ordinary Compose UI thread. No macOS missing-callback event was reproduced; the non-cancellable wait and timeout behavior are source-confirmed. Avoid waiting on the AppKit main queue through any new entry point.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Cancel scope while picker open and verify prompt cleanup without occupying an IO worker until timeout.
- Repeated requests, unavailable keyWindow/contentView, timeout, spurious wake and late callback.
- Stress a bounded pool and assert exactly-once terminal result with balanced native lifetime.

title: [Medium][NATIVE-031] Desktop native share extraction uses one mutable filename across versions, architectures and processes
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-031 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-031
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-share`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-share/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/platform/NativeLibLoader.kt:47-84`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/platform/NativeLibLoader.kt#L47-L84) — `cache directory/extraction/System.load`

## Root cause
Resources are OS/architecture-specific but every version/architecture extracts into the same per-user basename. Atomic move prevents partially written files, but there is no lock or immutable content-addressed identity between move and System.load. mkdirs results/ownership/symlink constraints are not validated.

## Impact and preconditions
Concurrent JVMs or versions may load the other process artifact; architecture changes can collide. Windows can refuse replacing a DLL already loaded by another process, forcing a fallback. A writable/redirected cache/system library path is a trust boundary, but same-user control alone is not a demonstrated privilege escalation.

## Supporting evidence
- ResourcePath includes osPart/archPart at47; targetFile uses only libFileName at60.
- Source performs mutable rename then loads path at84 with no intervening identity check.
- calf-file-picker has a newer immutable content-hashed NativeLibCache (commit befc455); the equivalent share loader was not migrated to that cache strategy.

## Recommended solution
Use version/OS/architecture/content-digest immutable filenames in a verified private cache directory; validate bytes/path, extract atomically without overwriting loaded versions, and document cleanup. Preserve intentional System.loadLibrary-first support for external packagers as an explicit trusted override. Reuse/adapt the content-addressed NativeLibCache already implemented in calf-file-picker rather than duplicating a new extraction design.

## Risks and compatibility
No wrong-binary or arbitrary-code execution was performed. The move-to-load race and Windows replacement outcome depend on concurrent launches/platform rules; cache and native library trust should be tested without claiming an exploitable CVE.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Two versions/architectures race between extraction and loading and each receives its own digest.
- Concurrent Windows process with loaded DLL does not lose native functionality.
- Read-only home, failed mkdirs, symlinked cache, interrupted extraction, no resource and trusted external packager library.

- None identified.

## Classification

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-share/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/ShareLauncher.android.kt:26-30`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/ShareLauncher.android.kt#L26-L30) — `share launch try/catch`
- [`calf-share/src/jsMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/WebShareApi.js.kt:45-55`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/src/jsMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/WebShareApi.js.kt#L45-L55) — `handleSharePromise`
- [`calf-share/src/wasmJsMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/WebShareApi.wasmJs.kt:10-18,29-37,48-54,64-70`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-share/src/wasmJsMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/share/WebShareApi.wasmJs.kt#L10-L18) — `then/catch chains`

## Root cause
Android includes currentOnResult(Success) inside the try that handles startActivity; a callback exception is caught as a launch failure and the callback is invoked again with Unavailable. Browser promise.then invokes the callback before a trailing catch that treats the callback exception as a share rejection and invokes another outcome.

## Impact and preconditions
One operation can produce conflicting duplicate results; user bugs are hidden as platform failures and destructive callback side effects can repeat. A second throwing invocation may escape in a different place as an unhandled error.

## Supporting evidence
- Android currentOnResult at28 lies inside catch Exception. JS/Wasm append catch after then handlers that invoke callbacks.

## Recommended solution
Catch only platform operation errors, then invoke user callbacks outside that catch boundary. Use promise.then(onFulfilled,onRejected) or equivalent separate settlement handling so result callback exceptions are not remapped to share outcomes.

## Risks and compatibility
Application callbacks are normally expected not to throw, but library error boundaries must not manufacture a second terminal platform event. Preserve crash reporting for the original application exception.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Callback deliberately throws after recording Success; exactly one callback invocation is observed.
- Platform start/share rejection invokes one failure and is distinct from callback failure.
- JS/Wasm resolved/rejected promises and Android ActivityNotFoundException paths.

- None identified.

title: [Medium][NATIVE-037] Replacing WebViewState or native lifecycle callbacks at the same composable identity is not safely rebound
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NATIVE-037 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NATIVE-037
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-webview`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/web/WebView.android.kt:151-162,190-215`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/web/WebView.android.kt#L151-L162) — `state reference, client rebind and AndroidView factory`
- [`calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.desktop.kt:50-108,110-141`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/desktopMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.desktop.kt#L50-L108) — `Unit-keyed DisposableEffect and factory captures`
- [`calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt:63-80,111-135`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.ios.kt#L63-L80) — `state reference and UIKitView factory`
- [`calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt:43-50,69-105`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/webMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebView.web.kt#L43-L50) — `state reference and iframe factory listeners`

## Root cause
Native view creation occurs once in interop factories/effects; effects read the native reference from the currently supplied state, but a replacement WebViewState starts with null. Factories do not rerun or transfer the native view when state changes. Several listeners/onCreated/onDispose lambdas capture the original state/navigator/callback because effects are Unit-keyed or factories are one-shot.

## Impact and preconditions
Passing a new state object to an existing WebView composition can leave the rendered old view attached while new content/navigation/evaluation has no native target. Desktop/iOS/Web listeners can keep updating the old state or navigator; callback substitution is not consistently observed.

## Supporting evidence
- Android updates client.state on each composition but assigns state.webView only in factory; Desktop initialization effect is keyed Unit.
- iOS factory installs navigationDelegate=state once; browser event listeners close over initial state/navigator.

## Recommended solution
Either explicitly key the native view lifecycle on its state owner, with proper disposal, or implement safe rebinding/update callbacks and rememberUpdatedState for callbacks. Document one-state-per-native-view ownership and behavior of navigator replacement.

## Risks and compatibility
The normal rememberWebViewState helper retains one state, so ordinary URL recomposition is not this failure. This is a source-traced edge case requiring Compose interop tests, not a claim every recomposition breaks WebView.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria

## Classification

- **Estimated complexity:** M

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-webview/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebSettings.kt:99-103`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/ui/web/WebSettings.kt#L99-L103) — `AndroidSettings.supportMultipleWindows default`
- [`calf-webview/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/web/WebView.android.kt:104-106,233-239,309-328`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-webview/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/web/WebView.android.kt#L104-L106) — `settings and AccompanistWebChromeClient`

## Root cause
supportMultipleWindows defaults true and is applied to Android WebSettings, but the installed WebChromeClient implements only title, icon and progress callbacks. It never overrides onCreateWindow; Android defaults reject creation. The public common WebView API also does not accept a custom chrome client.

## Impact and preconditions
Pages using target=_blank or window.open can request a new window that is never displayed, even with javaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically=true. Browser/payment/login flows depending on popup navigation can silently fail.

## Supporting evidence
- AccompanistWebChromeClient overrides only onReceivedTitle, onReceivedIcon, onProgressChanged.
- AndroidSettings defaults supportMultipleWindows=true; native applySettings calls setSupportMultipleWindows.

## Recommended solution
Choose and document a safe popup policy: reject explicitly, load allowed same-view requests, or expose/manage child windows with a trusted host callback. Do not enable multiple-window support without a handler and do not automatically open untrusted external schemes.

## Risks and compatibility
Source confirms the missing handler/configuration mismatch; exact Android link fallback behavior is WebView/version/content-dependent and needs device reproduction. Creating windows adds origin, lifecycle and phishing concerns; policy must be explicit.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- target=_blank link and user-initiated/scripted window.open with JavaScript/settings combinations.
- Accepted and denied popup origins/schemes yield documented outcomes.
- Child window closure, back navigation and dispose release all resources.

## Classification
- **Finding:** NAV-003
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-navigation`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt:10-26`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt#L10-L26) — `NavArgument/defaultValue/putDefaultValue`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt:74-126`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt#L74-L126) — `NavArgument.Builder`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt:138-146`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt#L138-L146) — `missingRequiredArguments`

## Root cause
build() unconditionally requires defaultValue != null, even if a type was supplied, and NavArgument stores defaultValue as non-null Any. setDefaultValue accepts Any? but build never verifies compatibility with the declared type.

## Impact and preconditions
A valid typed required argument without a default cannot be constructed; a nullable String argument cannot explicitly default to null. An Int type with a String default builds and then throws ClassCastException from putDefaultValue. The missing-required-arguments helper cannot be reached through a normal default-absent builder configuration.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- JVM baseline reproductions compiled with cached Kotlin2.4.20 and exited0: first three named checks reproduce these defects.
- Evidence: docs/testing/evidence/navigation-core-icons/{Repro.kt,run_jvm_repros.py,jvm-repro-result.txt}.
- Compiler also warns that defaultValue?.hashCode() line66 uses an unnecessary safe call, consistent with the non-null field.

## Recommended solution
Represent default absence separately from an explicit null; permit declared types without defaults; reject incompatible defaults at construction and handle nullable defaults consistently. Keep required-argument detection separate from per-value verification.

## Risks and compatibility
Avoid relying on unchecked generic casts or platform-specific reflection to implement common type validation. Existing callers might rely on delayed failure, so document the fail-fast change.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Typed Int without default builds and is required.
- Nullable String with explicit null builds and retains defaultValuePresent=true.
- Nonnullable Int with null or String default rejects at build, not later.
- All built-in scalar and array defaults, missing-required predicate and verify behavior are covered on JVM/JS/Wasm/Native.

## Classification

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveBaseBundle.kt:42-61`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveBaseBundle.kt#L42-L61) — `operator get<T>`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveBaseBundle.kt:94-109`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveBaseBundle.kt#L94-L109) — `putObject`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveBaseBundle.kt:556-582`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveBaseBundle.kt#L556-L582) — `getString overloads`

## Root cause
The generic get uses an erased as? T without a reified/type-token check, so JVM caller casts can throw despite the documented null-on-wrong-type behavior. getString calls toString on any value. putObject recognizes fewer types than the bundle's explicit setters, including omission of Float.

## Impact and preconditions
A wrong-type lookup may crash or silently coerce data rather than returning null/default. Generic insertion rejects values that explicit insertion supports. These inconsistencies impede reliable argument validation and migrations.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Baseline JVM checks reproduce wrong-type generic-get ClassCastException, Int-to-String coercion and putObject(Float) rejection.
- Specific primitive getters instead use explicit as? checks with default fallback, e.g. getDouble lines551-553.

## Recommended solution
Use well-defined typed accessors or a portable checked type strategy; align getString with its contract; decide and test the supported generic put set. Document this as an in-memory mutable map, not an Android Parcelable/PersistableBundle replacement.

## Risks and compatibility
Array/list values and mMap are exposed mutable references; deep-copy/thread-safety semantics are not currently provided. Kotlin/JS and Native generic-cast behavior must be tested rather than inferred from the JVM run.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Wrong-type get<Int> from a String follows the chosen contract without an unexpected caller ClassCastException.
- getString of Int42 returns the documented fallback/null rather than "42".
- All explicitly supported scalar/array/list setters have consistent generic insertion and retrieval rules.
- Explicit null versus absent key, aliasing and mutation behavior are documented/tested.

## Classification

- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt:580-594`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt#L580-L594) — `StringType.parseValue/serializeAsValue`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt:604-625`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt#L604-L625) — `StringArrayType`

## Root cause
String-array inference is commented out even though StringArrayType exists; custom Parcelable/Serializable lookup is entirely commented. String serialization leaves URI delimiters unescaped despite its KDoc, uses "null" for null and literal "null", and arrays inherit object toString serialization rather than an array codec.

## Impact and preconditions
Supported explicit String arrays fail inferred construction; string values lose distinctions on parse/serialize and can violate a caller's URI encoding expectations. Array serialized values cannot be used to reconstruct the original arrays. These are helper-API defects, not an active deep-link injection exploit: the host does not currently parse routes.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Baseline JVM repro confirms StringArray inference throws while explicit StringArrayType put/get works.
- Baseline JVM repro confirms serializeAsValue("a/b?x=1&n=2#frag") returns the unescaped input.
- Array append copies appear at lines363-364,431-432,486-487,549-550,624-625.

## Recommended solution
Specify a small portable type/codec contract, implement consistent inference including String arrays, define null versus literal encoding and round-trip serialization, and remove unsupported Parcelable/XML claims. If URI encoding belongs in another layer, state that clearly and change the misleading contract.

## Risks and compatibility
Encoding changes can break stored routes and must not double-encode already encoded data. Adding runtime reflection to common code would sacrifice multiplatform compatibility. Repeated array parseValue(previous) calls allocate copies and are O(n²) across n values.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- StringArray inference succeeds for empty and nonempty arrays and rejects mixed arrays.
- Round-trip null, literal "null", Unicode, slash/query/hash/ampersand characters and every supported array type.
- Unknown/custom fromArgType fails with a truthful supported-types error.
- Benchmark/bound repeated-array parsing before adopting it for large external inputs.

## Classification

- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-navigation`
- **Estimated complexity:** M

- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHost.kt:13-31`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHost.kt#L13-L31) — `AdaptiveNavHost remember/LaunchedEffect`

## Root cause
The graph builder is remembered without keys, and initialization is a LaunchedEffect(Unit). Recomposition with another controller, startDestination or builder does not rebuild graph closures or rerun start-route setup.

## Impact and preconditions
Replacing an empty controller at the same composition location can render no destination indefinitely; remembered destination lambdas can still capture the previous controller or stale state. Callers cannot infer the graph lifetime contract from the signature.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Keyless remember at line23 closes over the initial builder.
- LaunchedEffect(Unit) at line29 runs on host entry, not on controller replacement.

## Recommended solution
Choose and document static versus dynamic graph ownership. Key controller initialization correctly; use stable graph specifications and updated callback/state capture or intentional graph keys. Add replacement tests before exposing navigation as supported.

## Risks and compatibility
Blindly keying on an unstable builder lambda may rebuild the graph on every recomposition and lose state. Changing startDestination must not unexpectedly reset an existing stack.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Replace a controller at one composition site and verify initialization and callback routing.
- Recompose after an outer callback/state changes and confirm graph content sees intended values.
- Change startDestination with an empty and nonempty stack under an explicit policy.

- [`calf-navigation/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AndroidBackHandler.ios.kt:5-11`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AndroidBackHandler.ios.kt#L5-L11) — `iOS no-op back handler`
- [`calf-navigation/build.gradle.kts:1-23`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/build.gradle.kts#L1-L23) — `prototype module configuration`

## Root cause
The expect NavHostController is AndroidX on Android and Adaptive elsewhere, while the public rememberNavController and AdaptiveNavHost use Adaptive on every platform. Non-Android AndroidBackHandler actuals are no-ops and no browser/native stack adapter exists.

## Impact and preconditions
Consumers may assume AndroidX lifecycle/back-stack ownership, iOS native interactive gestures or browser history support that the Adaptive API does not implement. The module is included but intentionally not published and was described as coming soon.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- All ten navigation actual files were read; desktop/iOS/JS/Wasm back handlers explicitly contain only no-op comments.
- The actual controller extensions delegate to existing member methods; there is no evidence of infinite recursion from their same-named calls.
- Navigation build lacks module.publication.

## Recommended solution
Keep navigation experimental/unpublished. Record an ADR selecting an adapter to a mature navigation library or a deliberately minimal independent stack; publish an explicit capability matrix and an API migration plan before implementation.

## Risks and compatibility
A rewrite during identity migration would create unnecessary compatibility and licensing risk. No-op platform behavior is source-confirmed, but absence of a promised advanced feature is tracked as an improvement rather than an invented runtime vulnerability.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Compile a common consumer using the supported controller factory/host API on every target.
- Android system/predictive back, iOS app-provided back/gesture behavior, desktop keyboard back and web history are tested according to the declared contract.
- Per-entry lifecycle/viewmodel/restoration requirements are specified before release.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

title: [Medium][NAV-010] CupertinoIcon leaves the private-use glyph Text semantics exposed
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NAV-010 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NAV-010
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-cupertino-icons`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-cupertino-icons/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/cupertino/icons/CupertinoIcon.kt:43-83`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-cupertino-icons/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/cupertino/icons/CupertinoIcon.kt#L43-L83) — `CupertinoIcon semantics and Text`

## Root cause
The icon is a Material Text displaying a private-use character. A null contentDescription adds no semantics modifier, leaving the Text node; a non-null description adds parent image semantics without clearing the child text semantics.

## Impact and preconditions
Decorative icons are not reliably excluded from accessibility output, and labeled icons can retain a meaningless glyph-text node. The source-level semantics issue is confirmed; exact VoiceOver/TalkBack utterances and merged-node behavior were not executed here.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Lines55-62 only set contentDescription/Role.Image when non-null.
- The child Text at lines70-83 always uses iconChar; no clearAndSetSemantics or equivalent text suppression exists.
- All bundled codepoints are BMP and map to nonzero glyphs, so malformed catalogue codepoints are not the cause.

## Recommended solution
Implement explicit decorative-versus-labeled icon semantics, suppressing the glyph Text semantics while retaining one meaningful image description where provided. Follow Compose semantics guidance and test both merged/unmerged trees and real assistive technology.

## Risks and compatibility
Unconditionally clearing outer semantics could erase a caller's click action or label. Font glyph presence tests do not establish accessibility correctness.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- A null-description icon contributes no readable PUA text semantics.
- A labeled icon contributes one image label and no additional glyph announcement.
- Icons inside buttons preserve the button action/label in merged and unmerged trees.
- Run TalkBack, VoiceOver and desktop/browser accessibility checks at different font scales.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/pull/511

title: [Medium][NAV-011] Generated icon/symbol catalogues lack a reproducible generator and Apple availability metadata
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NAV-011 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NAV-011
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `improvement` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-cupertino-icons`, `calf-ui`, `sample:common`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-cupertino-icons/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/cupertino/icons/CupertinoIcons.kt:3-12`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-cupertino-icons/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/cupertino/icons/CupertinoIcons.kt#L3-L12) — `generated catalogue header/object`
- [`calf-ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/sf/symbols/SFSymbol.kt:3-20`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/sf/symbols/SFSymbol.kt#L3-L20) — `generated SF symbol names`
- [`sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/CupertinoIconsCatalogData.kt:1-30`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/CupertinoIconsCatalogData.kt#L1-L30) — `sample catalogue data`
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/ImageUtils.kt:36-40`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/ImageUtils.kt#L36-L40) — `UIKitImage.SystemName resolution`

## Root cause
Generated declarations claim SF/Cupertino coverage but the repository contains no generator/source manifest capable of reproducing names, aliases, categories and version mapping. SF names cover versions1.0-7.0 without per-symbol minimum-OS/variant/fallback metadata.

## Impact and preconditions
Future updates cannot be mechanically reviewed against a canonical source, and newer Apple names may resolve to no system image on older supported OS versions. This is not proof of an unconditional crash: the underlying UIImage lookup is nullable.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Persistent catalogue-result.json:1322 Cupertino declarations,1234 distinct codepoints, all covered by the font;1322 unique sample entries;6984 unique SF identifiers and values.
- The parser validates every declaration, including Kotlin escaped identifiers repeat/case/return; zero unparsed declarations.
- Git history reviewed for PRs510,511,514 does not introduce a generator.

## Recommended solution
Store generator code, pinned permitted input provenance and deterministic outputs; keep Cupertino font and Apple system name catalogues distinct. Add per-symbol availability or documented fallback/feature detection at the UIKit boundary.

## Risks and compatibility
Apple artwork licensing is separate from identifier strings. Font/codepoint validation proves mapping consistency, not glyph meaning, visual layout or OS availability of SF names.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Regenerate all catalogues deterministically with zero unexplained diff.
- Retain checks for unique identifiers, aliases, valid referenced names and cmap coverage.
- Resolve representative/newest SF names on oldest/current supported iOS versions with a deliberate missing-symbol fallback.
- Render glyph snapshots and check icon alignment, tint and accessibility.

## Dependencies
- NAV-009

## Historical context
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/pull/510

title: [Medium][NAV-012] Sample secure password text field logs every entered value
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NAV-012 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NAV-012
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `sample:common`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/AlertDialogScreen.kt:248-265`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/AlertDialogScreen.kt#L248-L265) — `AlertDialogIosTextField callbacks`

## Root cause
The password example sets isSecure=true but its onValueChange prints "Password: $it". The adjacent name field also prints user-entered text.

## Impact and preconditions
Real values entered into the demonstration can appear in local/device diagnostic output; copying the example propagates an unsafe pattern. This is a local logging exposure, not evidence of remote exfiltration or an embedded secret.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- isSecure=true at line262 and println("Password: $it") at line264 are in the same text-field descriptor.

## Recommended solution
Remove value logging from secure/user-data examples. If feedback is useful, display a non-sensitive event/count and explicitly teach that secure rendering does not make logging safe.

## Risks and compatibility
Verification must use synthetic test strings, never an owner's actual password or log dump. Avoid overclassifying a demo log as a remote attack.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Type a synthetic password and confirm its bytes never appear in captured test logs.
- Source assertion prevents interpolation of secure-field content into logging calls.
- Verify secure keyboard/display behavior separately on an iOS device.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

- None identified.

title: [Medium][NAV-013] Sample image export runs unbounded reads and image allocations without error or concurrency control
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NAV-013 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NAV-013
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `sample:common`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/FileSaverScreen.kt:169-185`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/FileSaverScreen.kt#L169-L185) — `export button coroutine`
- [`sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/FileSaverScreen.kt:214-245`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/FileSaverScreen.kt#L214-L245) — `circleCropImage`
- [`sample/common/src/androidMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/utils/ImageBitmapExt.android.kt:8-12`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/androidMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/utils/ImageBitmapExt.android.kt#L8-L12) — `PNG encode`
- [`sample/common/src/nonAndroidMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/utils/ImageBitmapExt.nonAndroid.kt:8-16`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/nonAndroidMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/utils/ImageBitmapExt.nonAndroid.kt#L8-L16) — `Skia encode`
- [`sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/ImagePickerScreen.kt:125-135`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/ImagePickerScreen.kt#L125-L135) — `eager selected-image list`

## Root cause
The export click launches in the composition scope, reads the entire file before switching to Default, then fully decodes/crops/encodes with no size/dimension cap, busy guard or exception handler. Android/JVM/iOS readByteArray actuals perform synchronous I/O. Non-Android encoding force-unwraps nullable data; selected images are all composed in a scrolling Column.

## Impact and preconditions
Large/corrupt/inaccessible inputs can freeze UI work, fail the coroutine or require several simultaneous full-size buffers; rapid clicks duplicate work. OOM magnitude and Skia resource lifetime are risks needing profiling, not measured leaks in this audit. Large multi-selection can also create excessive concurrent image work.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- readByteArray at line173 precedes withContext(Default) at174; no catch or in-flight state surrounds the launch.
- circleCropImage holds input bytes, a full source bitmap, a square output and encoded PNG; source.width/height directly determine allocation.
- Android encoder ignores Bitmap.compress Boolean; non-Android encodeToData uses !! and no explicit close on the temporary Image/Data.
- Cross-module source references: KmpFile.android.kt30-37, desktop.kt12, ios.kt35-42; synchronous reading despite suspend signatures.
- Cross-review boundary: IO-021 tracks library/Coil eager reads and API scheduling guidance; NAV-013 tracks the sample's distinct export orchestration, overlapping jobs, image allocations/encoder errors and eager preview list.

## Recommended solution
Separate I/O/CPU dispatch appropriately, bound input and decoded dimensions, downsample before crop, serialize/cancel exports, surface recoverable errors and retain CancellationException. Check encoder success/null results and deterministic release of owned native resources. Use a lazy bounded image list.

## Risks and compatibility
Dispatchers.Default is not a universal nonblocking-I/O guarantee, especially in browsers. Do not close Compose-owned bitmaps accidentally. Picker/saver native resource bugs are covered by the I/O audit rather than duplicated here.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Corrupt/empty/revoked/large-dimension images fail gracefully without crashing or leaking handles.
- Rapid repeated export and navigation away cancel/serialize work correctly.
- Measure peak memory and UI responsiveness on representative Android/iOS/JVM devices and browsers.
- Encoder failure and multi-select hundreds-of-images paths have bounded work and lazy rendering.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- None identified.
